### 

# Social Comments in Conversations

Social Comments in Conversations brings comments from your social media posts directly into the **Conversations** inbox. Instead of switching between Social Planner and individual social platforms, your team can view and respond to comments from the same place where you already manage SMS, email, and DMs.

When comment sync is enabled, each commenter is saved as a contact and their comment appears as a conversation thread with the original post for context. Your team can reply publicly, continue the conversation through a private DM, or use workflows to automatically follow up with potential leads.    Pasted markdown

> **Important:** Enabling Social Comments also creates a contact for every new commenter. Contact creation cannot be disabled separately while comment sync is enabled.

---

## Who Is This For?

Social Comments in Conversations is useful for:

- **Agency admins** managing social media for multiple clients
- **Sales teams and reps** handling inbound social leads
- **Businesses** using Social Planner to publish social content
- Teams that want to turn social engagement into conversations, leads, and opportunities    Pasted markdown

---

## How Social Comments Work

Once comment sync is enabled, comments from your connected social accounts are automatically brought into the **Conversations → Team Inbox**.

For each comment:

1. The commenter is created as a new contact.
2. The comment appears as a conversation in the Team Inbox.
3. The original post is displayed at the top of the conversation for context.
4. Your team can reply publicly to the comment or send a private DM.
5. Existing workflows can also trigger follow-up actions based on the comment.

### 

**Note:**Only comments on posts **published through Social Planner** are synced. Comments on posts that were published directly from Facebook, Instagram, or another social platform outside of Social Planner are not synced. This is a platform limitation.

---

# Prerequisites

Before enabling Social Comments, make sure:

- You are an **Agency Admin** or have the required admin access to the sub-account.
- At least one supported social account is connected through Social Planner.
- The **Conversations** module is active for the sub-account.

---

# Setting Up Social Comment Sync

#### 

### Step 1: Managing Social Comment Sync

Social Comment Sync is **enabled by default** for eligible sub-accounts. If you do not want social comments to appear in the Conversations inbox, you can disable comment sync at the **agency** or **sub-account** level.

### 

### Disable Comment Sync for a Sub-Account

To disable comment sync for an individual sub-account:

1. Go to **Agency Settings → Social Comments**.
2. Find the sub-account where you want to disable comment sync.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155082807489/original/YQeLcek55qYkaijv0s9X-LJEY07SN92IyQ.png?1791441914)

3. Turn **Comment Sync** off.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155082807511/original/OuY6ur4LhmqATe8DK-CG7pm-A3ZskleVJw.png?1791441941)

4. Review the confirmation prompt.

5. Click **Confirm** to apply the change.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155082807525/original/OS8kO5QjDIxfnFSvbwbgoHvhfe7137mhmw.png?1791441957)

Once disabled, **new social comments will no longer sync to Conversations** for that sub-account.

> **Note:** Disabling comment sync does not delete contacts or conversations that were created before sync was disabled. Existing conversations remain available in Conversations.

### 

### Disable Comment Sync for Multiple Sub-Accounts

Agency admins can also disable comment sync in bulk.

1. Go to **Agency Settings → Social Comments**.
2. Select the sub-accounts where you want to disable comment sync.
3. Select **Disable Comment Sync** from the bulk action bar![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155082807653/original/k5AQCOc1n4rYMLm1RnrPSg8qfQrodm7-mQ.png?1791442037)

4. Review the confirmation modal.

5. Click **Confirm**.

6. A success notification confirms the sub-accounts where the setting was updated.

### 

### 

### Disable Comment Sync at the Sub-Account Level

Users with the required sub-account permissions can also manage the setting from:

**Marketing → Social Planner → Settings → Comments**

Turn **Sync comments to conversations toggle** off to stop new social comments from appearing in Conversations.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155082812495/original/b3BGPrX94A6J9aa3dMQf1e2T5LULLdPBPw.png?1791445314)

### 

### What Happens When Comment Sync Is Disabled?

When comment sync is turned off:

- New social comments stop syncing to Conversations.
- Existing social comment conversations remain in the inbox.
- Existing contacts created from social comments are **not deleted**.
- Existing workflow automations are not deleted or modified.
- Comment management in Social Planner continues to work.
- You can turn comment sync back on whenever you want.

---

# Step 2: Configure Comment Settings at the Sub-Account Level

Comment settings are available in: **Marketing → Social Planner → Settings → Comments**

You can configure the following settings.

### 

### 1. Sync These Channels

Use the channel-level toggles to control which connected social platforms send comments to Conversations.

A platform without a connected account displays a **Connect account** option instead.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155082812687/original/p2z8FcWKC5uo-HNq8t-mbAKjVMNR9bCpkg.png?1791445445)

**At launch:** Facebook, Instagram Tiktok are supported.

Additional platforms are coming soon.

### 

### 2. Identify Social Leads

Add keywords that indicate potential buying intent, such as:

- `price`
- `interested`
- `available`
- `how much`

Comments containing these keywords can be surfaced at the top of the inbox when the relevant sort option is used.   There is not limit on adding keywords.

### Comments With Questions

Enable this option to prioritize comments containing a question mark.

For example:

> "How much does this cost?"

> "Do you ship to Texas?"

Question-based comments can be surfaced at the top because they may indicate higher purchase intent.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155082812793/original/BToW7H0WmBKjLIL-hC894GX_ipF4_70h7A.png?1791445519)

---

# Step 3: Complete the First-Time Setup in Conversations

The first time you open Conversations after enabling comment sync, a one-time setup modal explains the feature.

You can click on "Set up comment sync" and you will be redirected to Social Planner>> Settings to configure basis your requirements.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155082812848/original/BUBTf-8Y4zx5UbUTf2JFDyQGO0efLjhyZA.png?1791445560)

---

# Viewing Social Comments in Conversations

Once comment sync is enabled, social comments appear directly in the **Team Inbox** alongside your other conversations.

They are not placed in a separate inbox or tab.

Each social comment entry can show:

- Commenter's name or social handle
- Comment preview
- The post the comment was made on
- Social platform icon
- Timestamp

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155082813108/original/yOGuArqA8VTsetHzRedXfIXlCo4ETkCscg.png?1791445710)

### Filter for Social Comments

To view only social comment conversations:

1. Open the **Team Inbox**.
2. Click the **Social Comments** filter.
3. Your inbox will show only social comment threads.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155082813248/original/JfyeNfwqfSZfNmtfpawcGcv6I_Eu7sxdOg.png?1791445790)

---

# Opening a Social Comment

Click a social comment from the Team Inbox to open its conversation thread. The conversation view includes the original post and the comment.

## Post Card

The post card at the top of the conversation can include:

- Post thumbnail
- Post caption
- Social account name
- Social platform
- **View Post ↗** link to open the original post on the social platform

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155082813420/original/Md-PKSxrIFRFDLI57q2EKrjEdWKDZ2UI4A.png?1791445875)

## Contact Details

The right-side contact panel shows the contact created or matched for the commenter, including available:

- Name
- Social platform
- Tags
- Contact source
- Suggested actions

---

# Replying to Social Comments

You can respond directly from the conversation. Two reply options are available:

## 

## Public Reply

1. Use **Public Reply** to respond publicly underneath the original comment on the social platform.
2. Your reply is visible to other users who can see the original post and comment.
3. Platform-specific character and media limitations apply.

## 

## 

## Send DM

1. Use **Send DM** to continue the conversation privately with the commenter.
2. The private conversation moves into the main inbox as a standard DM thread, while the original comment thread displays a **Continued in DM** indicator.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155082813704/original/Awr9dugT4OP3kKBz-fIww5GuYdJAIzwesg.png?1791445989)

### Reply Limits

| Platform | Character Limit | Images Supported |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Facebook | No limit | Yes, up to 10 MB |
| Instagram | No limit | Yes, up to 10 MB |
| LinkedIn | 3,000 characters | No |
| TikTok | 150 characters | No |

---

# Identify and Prioritize High-Intent Social Leads

If one of your posts receives a large number of comments, use the available filtering and sorting tools to keep your inbox manageable.

You can:

1. Use **Social Comments** to view only social comment threads.

This allows your team to focus on potential leads without losing visibility into other engagement.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155082814704/original/FQx8gEtW_9brE2BYVON6_KEwZLY53vSXTg.png?1791446431)

- Add **buying-intent keywords** to prioritize relevant comments.
- Enable **Comments With Questions** to surface question

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155082814588/original/NLNV-GplkZ8EeIgUYLPM3JL3dJTNWmMu-w.png?1791446344)

---

# 

- Use the **Sort** option to bring higher-intent comments to the top.    Pasted markdown

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155082814872/original/ARNZqyzKi45iDc60JgJTUF8zXuI5JbC-og.png?1791446508)

# 

# Supported Platforms

According to the current release scope:

### Available at Launch

- Facebook
- Instagram
- TikTok

### Coming Soon

- LinkedIn
- YouTube
- Pinterest
- Threads
- Bluesky
- Community

# 

# Notes

**- TikTok:**Same as direct Instagram: the account syncs to the Integrations module, but messaging is disabled by default once enabled, direct inbound-outbound works no private DM support on Tiktok

- For Facebook connected through Social Planner, we will disable the the DM option by default and it's won't show as connected in integrations module.  
- To enable DM for social planner connections then we need to enable it from settings option.

# 

# Frequently Asked Questions

### **Will comments on posts I didn't publish through Social Planner be synced?**

No. Only comments on posts published through Social Planner are synced. Comments on posts published directly from Facebook, Instagram, or other platforms are not included.

### 

### **What happens if I turn comment sync off?**

New comments stop syncing. Existing contacts and conversations created before you disabled sync remain in place and are not deleted.

### 

### **Will my existing Facebook, Instagram and Tiktok comment workflows continue to work?**

Yes. Existing workflow triggers continue to work as before. Enabling comment sync does not change or break existing workflow behavior.

### 

### **Can the same person comment multiple times?**

Yes. Each comment appears as its own inbox entry, but comments from the same person are linked to the same contact record. Duplicate contacts are not created.

### **My social account connection expired. What should I do?**

Reconnect the affected social account from your Social Planner settings. Once the account is successfully reconnected, comment syncing can resume.

### 

### **Can I still manage comments from Social Planner?**

Yes. Social Comments in Conversations adds another way to view and respond to comments. Existing comment management functionality in Social Planner continues to be available.

title_en: How to Manage Event Refunds, Cancellations, and Check-In Eligibility
source_md:
Event Refunds & Cancellations make it easier to manage paid event registrations directly from the Events area in HighLevel. You can issue full or partial refunds, cancel registrations, combine both actions when needed, review refund history, and control QR code check-in based on payment status. These updates also improve event revenue reporting by reflecting the actual amount paid after discounts.

---

**TABLE OF CONTENTS**

- [What are Event Refunds & Cancellations?](#What-are-Event-Refunds-&-Cancellations?)
- [Key Benefits of Event Refunds & Cancellations](#Key-Benefits-of-Event-Refunds-&-Cancellations)
- [Refunds vs. Cancellations](#Refunds-vs.-Cancellations)
- [Initiating a Refund or Cancellation](#Initiating-a-Refund-or-Cancellation)
- [Full and Partial Refunds](#Full-and-Partial-Refunds)
- [Refunding Without Canceling the Registration](#Refunding-Without-Canceling-the-Registration)
- [Refunding and Canceling at the Same Time](#Refunding-and-Canceling-at-the-Same-Time)
- [Canceling a Registration Without Issuing a Refund](#Canceling-a-Registration-Without-Issuing-a-Refund)
- [What Happens When a Registration is Canceled?](#What-Happens-When-a-Registration-is-Canceled?)
- [Viewing Refund Status and Refund History](#Viewing-Refund-Status-and-Refund-History)
- [Accurate Event Revenue Reporting](#Accurate-Event-Revenue-Reporting)
- [QR Code Check-In by Payment Status](#QR-Code-Check-In-by-Payment-Status)
- [How To Manage Event Refunds and Cancellations](#How-To-Manage-Event-Refunds-and-Cancellations)
- [Frequently Asked Questions](#Frequently-Asked-Questions)
- [Related Articles](#Related-Articles)

---

# **What are Event Refunds & Cancellations?**

Event Refunds & Cancellations let you manage attendee payment and registration changes from the event’s **Registrations** area. Instead of moving between separate payment and event screens, you can refund, cancel, or combine both actions from the attendee record.

A **refund** returns money to the attendee.

A **cancellation** removes the active event registration.

These actions are related, but they are not the same. You can:

- refund without canceling,
- cancel without refunding,
- or refund and cancel at the same time.

---

## **Key Benefits of Event Refunds & Cancellations**

Managing refunds and registration changes from one place reduces manual steps and makes it easier to understand what happened to an attendee’s payment and ticket.

- **Faster refund management:** Issue refunds directly from the event registration.
- **Flexible refund options:** Process full or partial refunds.
- **Separate payment from attendance:** Refund an attendee without automatically canceling their registration.
- **Simpler cancellations:** Cancel a registration directly from the attendee Actions menu.
- **Clear refund visibility:** Review payment status and refund history from the registration record.
- **More accurate revenue:** Event revenue now reflects the actual amount paid after discounts.
- **Better check-in control:** Decide which payment statuses are allowed to check in by QR code.

---

## **Refunds vs. Cancellations**

Refunding and canceling affect different parts of an event registration. Understanding the difference helps you avoid unintentionally removing an attendee when you only meant to return money, or leaving a registration active when you intended to cancel it.

**Refunding a registration** returns money to the original payment method.

**Canceling a registration** affects the event registration itself. According to the cancellation warning shown in HighLevel:

- ticket seats return to inventory,
- QR passes stop working,
- the attendee is notified,
- the cancellation cannot be undone.

You can also choose to perform both actions together.

---

## **Initiating a Refund or Cancellation**

Refund and cancellation actions are available directly from the event’s **Registrations** tab. This keeps attendee management in the same place where you already review registrations and payment status.

From the attendee **Actions** menu, you can choose:

- **Initiate refund**
- **Cancel registration**

**![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155080109323/original/Y0pF_9JrMZlX3sqe3Hb1i8Jff_EvrfVvGw.png?1788525735)**

---

## **Full and Partial Refunds**

HighLevel supports both full and partial refunds for eligible event payments. This gives you flexibility when an attendee should receive only part of the amount back.

A **full refund** returns the full refundable amount.

A **partial refund** returns less than the full amount.

When you open the **Refund registration** window, you can:

- select the applicable ticket,
- adjust the amount,
- add optional notes,
- choose whether to also cancel the registration.

Refund notes are stored on the payment record and appear in refund history.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155080109621/original/HhUb5sBLJbRkjZJjb3Gjnz9wq8IL9ksjsw.png?1788525829)

---

## **Refunding Without Canceling the Registration**

Refunding without canceling is useful when you want to return money but still allow the attendee to remain registered. Because payment status and registration status are separate, a refunded attendee can remain active unless the registration is also canceled.

To refund without canceling:

1. Open the attendee **Actions** menu.
2. Select **Initiate refund**.
3. Choose the ticket or tickets to refund.
4. Enter the refund amount.
5. Add optional notes if needed.
6. Leave **Also cancel this registration** unchecked.
7. Click the refund button.

The refund is returned to the original payment method according to the connected payment processor’s timing.

The refund dialog may show an estimated arrival window, such as **4–6 business days**, but actual timing can vary by provider.

---

## **Refunding and Canceling at the Same Time**

Refunding and canceling together is useful when the attendee should receive their money back and no longer remain registered for the event. HighLevel combines both actions into one confirmation flow.

To refund and cancel:

1. Select **Initiate refund** from the attendee’s Actions menu.
2. Enter the refund amount.
3. Select **Also cancel this registration**.
4. Review the cancellation warning.
5. Confirm the combined action.

When cancellation is included:

- seats return to event inventory,
- QR passes stop working,
- the attendee is notified,
- the cancellation cannot be undone.

**![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155080115350/original/uDewkXSrXyzin3kuumX9Dmxq9a8Aqu1uQA.png?1788528268)**

---

## **Canceling a Registration Without Issuing a Refund**

Cancellation can be handled separately when you need to remove an attendee from the event without returning payment. This keeps registration status separate from payment status.

To cancel without refunding:

1. Open the attendee **Actions** menu.
2. Select **Cancel registration**.
3. Review the cancellation warning.
4. Enter an optional reason.
5. Leave **Also refund this registration** unchecked.
6. Click **Cancel registration**.

The optional reason is stored on the registration record and is not sent to the attendee.

**![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155080115629/original/9l4GB6nghQhJBlZWYjjU70dEAwSo9-VwfQ.png?1788528359)**

---

## **What Happens When a Registration is Canceled?**

Cancellation changes the attendee’s event access rather than only their payment. This makes it important to confirm the action before completing it.

When a registration is canceled:

- the ticket seat returns to inventory,
- the attendee’s QR passes stop working,
- the attendee is notified,
- the cancellation cannot be undone.

If you only need to return money and still want the attendee to remain registered, use the refund workflow without selecting the cancellation option.

---

## **Viewing Refund Status and Refund History**

Refund visibility makes it easier to confirm whether a refund was processed and understand the payment history for the registration. You can review this information from the attendee details instead of searching through a separate payment screen.

The **Payment details** area can show:

- order details,
- transaction details,
- order total,
- payment status,
- refund history,
- refund amount,
- refund status,
- refund date and time.

**![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155080115833/original/-kwuRfFq0VZt67MHUeqR8Di0U3r8Kp3S5A.png?1788528442)**

---

## **Accurate Event Revenue Reporting**

Event revenue now reflects what attendees actually paid, including discounts. This gives organizers a more reliable view of event performance and avoids overstating revenue when discounted tickets are sold.

Previously, revenue could be calculated using:

**ticket price × number of sales**

That could overstate total earnings when discounts were applied.

The updated calculation reflects the actual sale amount after discounts, giving you a more accurate picture of event revenue.

---

## **QR Code Check-In by Payment Status**

Payment-status check-in controls let you decide which attendees are allowed to check in by QR code. This is useful when refunded or partially refunded attendees should still be admitted in some cases.

In **Registration settings**, use **Payment statuses allowed for check-in** to choose which payment statuses can enter through QR code check-in.

The available options shown in HighLevel include:

- **Succeeded**
- **Partially refunded**
- **Refunded**

For example, if you select only **Succeeded**, attendees with refunded payments will not be allowed to check in by QR code.

If you also select **Refunded** or **Partially refunded**, those registrations can remain eligible for check-in based on the payment status settings.

**![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155080116275/original/ngVJ8uyh8LTd8DzPccoAP3m5Dm2B5UImLg.png?1788528549)**

---

## **How To Manage Event Refunds and Cancellations**

Using the registration Actions menu keeps refund and cancellation tasks in one place. Choose the workflow based on whether you need to return money, remove the registration, or do both.

### 

### **Step 1: Open Event Registrations**

1. Go to **Memberships > Events**.
2. Open the event.
3. Select the **Registrations** tab.
4. Find the attendee you want to manage.

### 

### **Step 2: Open the Actions Menu**

1. Click the attendee’s **Actions** menu.
2. Choose either:

   - **Initiate refund**, or
   - **Cancel registration**.

****![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155080116370/original/vEFJQC7nAoGYUS7XWg5aD6HREdFWhPifuQ.jpeg?1788528576)****

### 

### **Step 3: Issue a Refund**

1. Select **Initiate refund**.
2. Choose the ticket or tickets.
3. Enter the refund amount.
4. Add optional notes.
5. Leave **Also cancel this registration** unchecked if the attendee should remain registered.
6. Click the refund button.

**![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155080116397/original/aTh-EFCobwBY3TiKuAlZJT6Rrw8QpFY_2w.jpeg?1788528593)**

### 

### **Step 4: Issue a Partial Refund**

1. Open **Initiate refund**.
2. Select the applicable ticket.
3. Enter an amount lower than the full refundable amount.
4. Add optional notes if needed.
5. Confirm the refund.

The remaining registration stays active unless you also choose to cancel it.

### 

### **Step 5: Refund and Cancel Together**

1. Open **Initiate refund**.
2. Enter the refund amount.
3. Select **Also cancel this registration**.
4. Review the warning.
5. Confirm the action.

### 

### **Step 6: Cancel Without a Refund**

1. Open the attendee **Actions** menu.
2. Select **Cancel registration**.
3. Enter an optional reason.
4. Leave **Also refund this registration** unchecked.
5. Confirm the cancellation.

****![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155080116500/original/VECJF-Ml6Qao7xR0ybg4mZc1VkMtfPnneA.png?1788528643)****

### 

### **Step 7: Verify the Refund**

1. Open the attendee registration details.
2. Go to **Payment details**.
3. Review **Payment status**.
4. Check the **Refund history** section for the refund amount and status.

****![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155080116534/original/iQDunldNcwQMvjYOVfA2fWcOPyj52AlbWg.jpeg?1788528671)****

### 

### **Step 8: Configure QR Check-In Eligibility**

1. Open the event.
2. Go to **Settings**.
3. Select **Registration**.
4. Find **Payment statuses allowed for check-in**.
5. Select the payment statuses that should be allowed to use QR code check-in.
6. Save your changes.

****![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155080116565/original/tSpA4tqGGgjMDv8qajlG61hPCIgj5HyQUg.jpeg?1788528695)****

---

## **Frequently Asked Questions**

**Q: What is the difference between a refund and a cancellation?**  
A: A refund returns money to the attendee. A cancellation removes the active event registration.

**Q: Can I refund an attendee without canceling their registration?**  
A: Yes. Leave **Also cancel this registration** unchecked when processing the refund.

**Q: Can I cancel a registration without issuing a refund?**  
A: Yes. Use **Cancel registration** and leave **Also refund this registration** unchecked.

**Q: Can I issue a partial refund?**  
A: Yes. Enter a refund amount lower than the full refundable amount.

**Q: What happens to the ticket seat when I cancel a registration?**  
A: The seat returns to event inventory.

**Q: What happens to the attendee’s QR pass after cancellation?**  
A: The QR pass stops working.

**Q: Can I undo a canceled registration?**  
A: No. The cancellation warning states that the action cannot be undone.

**Q: How long does a refund take?**  
A: Refund timing depends on the connected payment processor. The refund dialog may show an estimated timeframe, such as 4–6 business days.

**Q: Can refunded attendees still check in?**  
A: Yes, if their payment status is included under **Payment statuses allowed for check-in** and the registration itself has not been canceled.

**Q: Where can I see whether a refund succeeded?**  
A: Open the attendee’s **Payment details** and review the payment status and refund history.

**Q: Does event revenue account for discounts?**  
A: Yes. The updated revenue calculation reflects the actual amount paid after discounts.

---

### **Related Articles**

- [How to Create and Manage Events in HighLevel](https://help.gohighlevel.com/en/support/solutions/articles/155000008071)
- [Check-in Experience for In Person Events](https://help.gohighlevel.com/en/support/solutions/articles/155000008294)
- [How to Manage Refunds within the CRM](https://help.gohighlevel.com/en/support/solutions/articles/48001238332)
- [Refund Workflow Trigger in HighLevel](https://help.gohighlevel.com/en/support/solutions/articles/155000003537)
- [How to Manually Add Attendees to Events in HighLevel](https://help.gohighlevel.com/en/support/solutions/articles/155000008421)
- [Events and Workflows Integration — Automate Event Journeys](https://help.gohighlevel.com/en/support/solutions/articles/155000008431)

title_en: How to Set Up Root Domain/Subdomain for Funnels/Websites
source_md:
Connecting a root domain or subdomain to HighLevel lets you publish Funnels, Websites, Stores, Blogs, and Webinars using your own branded web address. You can connect supported domains automatically with Domain Connect or configure the required DNS records manually. After connecting the domain, you can assign the correct landing page and configure default and 404/error pages to provide visitors with a consistent experience. This guide covers domain connection, DNS setup, page configuration, removal, and common troubleshooting steps.

# What Is a Root Domain or Subdomain in HighLevel?

A root domain is the primary web address for a site, such as `example.com`. A subdomain adds a prefix to the root domain, such as `www.example.com` or `offers.example.com`.

HighLevel lets you connect root domains and subdomains to supported Sites products so visitors can access Funnels, Websites, Stores, Blogs, and Webinars through a branded URL. Depending on your DNS provider, you can use Domain Connect or configure the required DNS records manually.

## Key Benefits of Connecting a Root Domain or Subdomain

Connecting the correct domain gives visitors a branded destination while allowing HighLevel to route traffic to the appropriate site content.

- **Branded Visitor Experience:** Publish HighLevel content using a domain or subdomain associated with your business.
- **Flexible Connection Options:** Use Domain Connect when supported or configure DNS manually when needed.
- **Automatic SSL:** HighLevel provisions SSL after the domain connects successfully.
- **Controlled Landing Experience:** Choose which Funnel step or Website page loads when visitors open the domain without an additional path.
- **Custom Error Handling:** Configure a branded 404/error page for visitors who open an unavailable URL.
- **Configuration Reminders:** Eligible connected domains can display an **Action Required** reminder when default-page configuration is incomplete.

## Prerequisites and Limitations

Preparing the domain and confirming where its DNS is managed helps prevent connection conflicts and reduces verification delays.

**Before you begin:**

- You must own or have access to the root domain or subdomain you want to connect.
- You need access to the active DNS provider when manual configuration is required.
- Decide whether visitors should use a root domain such as `example.com` or a subdomain such as `www.example.com` or `offers.example.com`.
- If the hostname currently supports another website or service that must remain active, use a different available subdomain instead of repointing it.

**Current limitations and behaviors:**

- A single hostname cannot point to multiple platforms or servers at the same time.
- Do not create both an A record and a CNAME record for the same hostname.
- If Cloudflare manages the DNS, set the HighLevel A or CNAME record to **DNS only**, not Proxied.
- DNS changes may require time to propagate and can take up to 24 hours.
- The **Action Required** reminder applies when an eligible connected domain is missing its default page or default 404/error page.
- The **Action Required** reminder appears only in the sub-account where the domain was originally connected.

```
Note: If you purchased the domain directly through HighLevel, you can manage its DNS records from the Purchased Domains area instead of signing in to an external registrar. Refer to Configure & Connect Purchased Domains for the appropriate setup workflow.
```

## How To Set Up a Root Domain or Subdomain

Connecting the domain in the correct order allows HighLevel to verify DNS, associate the address with your content, and provision SSL successfully.

### Step 1: Decide Whether to Use a Root Domain or Subdomain

Choosing the correct hostname before changing DNS helps prevent an existing website or service from being unintentionally replaced.

A root domain uses the primary address:

`example.com`

A subdomain adds a prefix:

`www.example.com`  
`offers.example.com`  
`go.example.com`

**Important:** If the root domain already hosts another website or service that must remain active, use an available subdomain instead of repointing the root domain.

### Step 2: Start the Domain Connection in HighLevel

Starting from the Domains area allows HighLevel to identify the type of Sites connection and provide the appropriate automatic or manual DNS workflow.

1. From the **Sub-Account** view, click **Settings**.
2. Select **Domains & URL Redirects**.
3. Click **+ Connect a domain**.
4. Locate **Funnel/Website/Store/Blog/Webinar** and click **Connect**.
5. Enter the root domain or subdomain in the **Domain URL** field.
6. Choose the connection method:
   - **Continue:** Attempt automatic setup with Domain Connect.
   - **Add record manually:** Configure the required DNS record yourself.

![Domain connection screen showing the Domain URL field and connection options](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155081934193/original/muqW-oNc1TuA6yl0jyGO1pGnxCf0k5HmJw.png?1790491150)

When connecting a root domain, HighLevel can also add the `www` version and configure a 301 redirect so traffic from the `www` address is sent to the root domain.

```
Note: The Connect a domain screen can also include other supported products, such as AI Studio. To connect a domain directly to an AI Studio project, select AI Studio → Connect and follow the AI Studio custom-domain workflow.
```

  

### Step 3: Configure the Domain Automatically or Manually

Use Domain Connect when automatic setup is supported by your DNS provider, or manually add the required DNS record when automatic configuration is unavailable or not preferred.

#### Automatic Setup with Domain Connect

Domain Connect can authorize a supported DNS provider and automatically create the records required for the connection.

1. Enter the domain in the connection flow and click **Continue**.
2. If HighLevel recognizes a supported provider, click **Authorize**.
3. Sign in to the domain provider when prompted.
4. Approve the requested DNS connection.
5. After authorization is complete, close the provider tab and return to HighLevel.
6. Allow HighLevel to verify the DNS configuration.

![Domain Connect authorization screen for a supported DNS provider](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155081934194/original/xTl7bK3vxo1_kaENf0c58nppkg4DYtT3HA.png?1790491171)

#### Manual DNS Setup

Manual setup lets you add the required record directly at the provider that currently manages the domain's DNS.

1. Enter the domain in HighLevel and click **Add record manually**.
2. Sign in to the provider managing the domain's active DNS.
3. Add one of the supported records shown below.

| Use Case | Type | Host / Name | Value / Target |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Root domain | **A** | `@` | `162.159.140.166` |
| Subdomain | **CNAME** | Subdomain only, such as `www` or `offers` | `sites.ludicrous.cloud` |
| Supported subdomain alternative | **A** | Subdomain only | `162.159.140.166` |

**Important:** Use an A record or CNAME for a supported subdomain configuration, not both for the same hostname. If you use Cloudflare, set the applicable A or CNAME record to **DNS only**.

![Manual DNS configuration showing the required domain record values](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155081933176/original/VRdAkUx76Uel-RcfwUyc8NHqDXMKIDytjA.png?1790486871)

### Step 4: Associate the Domain With Your Site Content

Associating the verified domain tells HighLevel which Funnel or Website content should load when visitors use that address.

1. Wait for HighLevel to verify the required DNS record.
2. On the domain association screen, select the applicable **Funnel** or **Website**.
3. Select the Funnel step or Website page that should act as the default landing page.
4. Click **Link Domain**.

HighLevel begins provisioning SSL automatically after the domain is connected. SSL can take a few minutes to complete.

![Domain association screen showing the site content selected for the connected domain](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155081933948/original/Sk3yZhm_VT6h8wKmex7_qFxnERX4koZuQA.png?1790490067)

### Step 5: Configure the Default Page and 404/Error Page

Default-page settings control what visitors see at the main domain and where they are sent when they request an invalid or unavailable URL.

1. Go to **Settings → Domains & URL Redirects**.
2. Locate the connected domain and click **Manage**.
3. Review the domain's **Connected Products**.
4. If an **Action Required** reminder appears, click it.
5. Select an eligible page from the **Default Page** dropdown.
6. Select an eligible page from the **Default 404/Error Page** dropdown.

![Connected Products screen showing the Action Required reminder for missing default page settings](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155081934079/original/kXLKvQ6Fu6NLymPaXia8-Ov7P1d4VrzVhQ.png?1790490589)
![Action Required modal showing the Default Page and Default 404 Error Page dropdowns](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155081934077/original/nwWcdEBEdalWmHpDaRGVMGQc3Hm7TOYUGQ.png?1790490574)

**Note:** The Action Required reminder appears only in the sub-account where the domain was originally connected.

You can also manage the default and 404/error page settings through the existing Edit Domain flow:

1. Go to **Settings → Domains & URL Redirects**.
2. Click **Manage** for the domain.
3. Open the three-dot menu for the applicable domain or connected product.
4. Select **Edit**.
5. Update the default page or **Set default 404/Error Page** setting.
6. Click **Save**.

![Edit Domain modal showing default page and default 404 error page settings](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155081934089/original/UgJbal1vh5-IWUX1zQw4CWKNRIazEnwMNg.png?1790490618)

## How To Check Your DNS Records

A public DNS lookup can help confirm whether the expected A or CNAME record has propagated before you continue troubleshooting the connection in HighLevel.

1. Open a public DNS lookup tool such as MXToolbox.
2. Select the applicable lookup type, such as a DNS or CNAME lookup.
3. Enter the root domain or subdomain you connected.
4. Run the lookup.
5. Confirm that the expected HighLevel record is publicly visible.

**CNAME:** `sites.ludicrous.cloud`

**A record:** `162.159.140.166`

**DNS propagation:** Recently changed DNS records may not appear immediately. Allow up to 24 hours before assuming the configuration has failed.

## How To Remove a Domain

Removing a domain disconnects it from the sub-account, so confirm that the address is no longer required for active site content before deleting the connection.

1. Go to **Settings → Domains & URL Redirects**.
2. Locate the domain and click **Manage**.
3. Open the three-dot menu.
4. Select **Delete**.
5. Confirm the deletion in the confirmation dialog.

![Domain management menu showing the Delete option](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155081933769/original/iJVuAZOrjhSj4zTjcoBj8sOr45R5TUXDMw.png?1790489416)

## Troubleshooting Domain Connection Issues

Most connection problems come from records being added at the wrong DNS provider, conflicting records, propagation delays, or Cloudflare proxy settings.

### HighLevel Cannot Find the CNAME or A Record

This error means HighLevel cannot detect the expected DNS record for the hostname being connected.

1. Confirm which provider hosts the domain's active DNS by checking the nameservers.
2. Make sure the DNS record was added at that provider.
3. Check whether the hostname already has an A or CNAME record pointing elsewhere.
4. Use only one supported record for the hostname:
   - CNAME → `sites.ludicrous.cloud`
   - A record → `162.159.140.166`
5. Enter only the hostname portion, such as `www` or `offers`, in the Host/Name field when required by the provider.
6. Save the DNS changes and allow time for propagation.
7. Return to HighLevel and retry verification.

### The Domain Shows an SSL or Privacy Error

SSL cannot complete reliably when HighLevel cannot verify the hostname or when conflicting DNS records send traffic to different destinations.

- Remove conflicting A or CNAME records for the hostname.
- Confirm the required HighLevel A or CNAME record exists.
- Review unexpected records that point the hostname to another platform.
- If you use Cloudflare, make sure the HighLevel record is set to **DNS only**.
- After correcting DNS, allow time for propagation and SSL provisioning.
- Check for unexpected AAAA records or other DNS records that may route the hostname somewhere other than HighLevel. Conflicting DNS records can interfere with domain verification or SSL provisioning.

### A Cloudflare Domain Does Not Connect Correctly

Cloudflare proxying can prevent HighLevel from validating the A or CNAME record used for Funnels and Websites.

1. Sign in to Cloudflare.
2. Open the affected domain and go to **DNS**.
3. Locate the A or CNAME record used for HighLevel.
4. Change **Proxy status** to **DNS only**.
5. Save the change.
6. Return to HighLevel and retry the connection after DNS updates.

![Cloudflare DNS record with Proxy status configured as DNS only](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155081933747/original/ralB03T3FvpLE46-NepK24vLLNbMDctg5w.png?1790489290)

### The Domain Sometimes Shows a 404 Page

Intermittent 404 behavior can occur when different domain versions route inconsistently or when the domain does not have the intended default-page configuration.

- Check whether visitors are using both the root and `www` versions of the domain.
- Configure the appropriate 301 redirect when one version should always send visitors to the other.
- Confirm that the intended Funnel step or Website page is configured as the default page.
- Configure a **Default 404/Error Page** so invalid paths lead to the intended branded error page.

## Frequently Asked Questions

Q: Can I add the same domain to more than one sub-account within my agency?

Yes. HighLevel supports adding the same domain to multiple sub-accounts within the same agency.

Q: How many domains can I add to a sub-account?

HighLevel does not currently specify a limit on the number of domains that can be added.

Q: Do I need to purchase an SSL certificate separately?

No. HighLevel automatically provisions SSL after the domain is connected successfully.

Q: Can more than one Funnel or Website use the same domain?

Yes. Multiple Funnels and Websites can use the same domain in HighLevel. Configure the applicable paths and default-page behavior so each URL routes visitors correctly.

Q: Can I purchase a domain directly through HighLevel?

Yes. Eligible accounts can purchase and manage domains through HighLevel's Domain Purchase experience.

Q: Can I manually configure DNS instead of using Domain Connect?

Yes. Manual DNS setup remains available if you prefer to manage the records yourself or your DNS provider does not support automatic Domain Connect.

title_en: How to use Custom Fields for Opportunities
source_md:
Custom Fields for Opportunities give you the flexibility to tailor your CRM to match your exact sales process. By creating, organizing, and applying custom fields, you can track details that matter most to your business—from sales deadlines and client preferences to budgets and lead sources. These fields also integrate seamlessly with filtering, reporting, and pipeline customization, helping your team focus on the right opportunities.

---

**TABLE OF CONTENTS**

- [What is Custom Fields for Opportunities?](#What-is-Custom-Fields-for-Opportunities?)
- [Key Benefits of Custom Fields for Opportunities](#Key-Benefits-of-Custom-Fields-for-Opportunities)
- [How to Create and Manage Custom Fields](#How-to-Create-and-Manage-Custom-Fields)
- [Creating New Custom Field](#Creating-New-Custom-Field)
- [Creating a Folder](#Creating-a-Folder)
- [Managing Custom Fields](#Managing-Custom-Fields)
- [Using Custom Fields in Opportunities Dashboard](#Using-Custom-Fields-in-Opportunities-Dashboard)
- [Display Custom Fields on Opportunity Cards](#Display-Custom-Fields-on-Opportunity-Cards)
- [Frequently Asked Questions](#Frequently-Asked-Questions)
- [Related Articles](#Related-Articles)

---

[동영상](https://www.youtube.com/embed/Ti7BYY47ntM?&wmode=opaque)

---

# **What is Custom Fields for Opportunities?**

Custom Fields for Opportunities allow you to add, manage, and organize additional data points in your sales pipeline beyond the default fields provided by HighLevel. This feature ensures your pipeline reflects the unique aspects of your business process.

You can create text, dropdown, date, monetary, and other field types, categorize them into folders, and even hide empty fields for a cleaner view. These fields then become usable in filtering, reporting, and automation to streamline workflows.

---

# **Key Benefits of Custom Fields for Opportunities**

Custom Fields give you control over how you track and organize opportunities, making your CRM a more powerful tool.

- **Personalization:** Capture information specific to your business, such as budget, preferences, or product details.

- **Organization:** Group fields into folders and reorder them for easier data management.

- **Efficiency:** Use the “hide empty fields” option to keep pipeline views clean and focused.

- **Better Reporting:** Include custom fields in dashboards, widgets, and reports for deeper insights.

- **Filtering Power:** Filter and sort opportunities by custom criteria to quickly prioritize leads.

- **Automation:** Use custom fields in workflows, campaigns, and merge fields to save time.

---

# **How to Create and Manage Custom Fields**

Creating and managing custom fields ensures your team captures the right details for every opportunity.

### **Accessing Custom Fields**

There are two ways to reach the Custom Fields dashboard in HighLevel. Both methods take you to the same place, so you can choose whichever is more convenient.

**Via Settings**

From your sub-account dashboard, open the **Settings** menu and scroll down to select **Custom Fields**. This will take you directly to the Custom Fields dashboard.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155054373293/original/1GqOozmZr8R05rcBS02bYcwmABW5_Kvg-g.png?1758625175)

**Via Opportunity**

Inside the **Opportunities** section, select any existing opportunity and click **Add/Manage Fields**. This shortcut redirects you to the same Custom Fields dashboard, making it quick to edit while reviewing an opportunity.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155054373315/original/GbQRrMA_9OgqCGYdKxEYDxnrdnGKI_MFTQ.png?1758625198)

---

## **Creating New Custom Field**

Creating custom fields allows you to capture details unique to your sales process directly within opportunities. From client budgets to follow-up dates, these fields give you the flexibility to customize your pipeline and ensure important information is always tracked.

### **Add Field**

Click the **+ Add Field** button at the top right of the Custom Fields dashboard. This begins the process of creating a new custom field for opportunities or other objects.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155054374744/original/bS4xfntd-FcxoDXa0dTIyuGnQaFO1W7cJg.png?1758625895)

### **Choose Field Type**

Select from various field types to match your data needs. Options include **text inputs** (single line, multi-line, list), **values** (number, phone, monetary), **choices** (dropdowns, radio, checkbox), **date/time** (date picker), and **other inputs** like file upload or signature.

| **Field Type** | **Example Use Case** |
| --- | --- |
| **Single Line** | Enter the project name or client company name. |
| **Multi Line** | Add detailed notes about client requirements. |
| **Text Box List** | Track multiple product SKUs associated with an opportunity. |
| **Number** | Record a probability score for conversion (e.g., 80%). |
| **Phone** | Save an alternate decision-maker’s phone number. |
| **Monetary** | Store the client’s budget or estimated deal value. |
| **Dropdown (Single)** | Select the sales stage (e.g., Negotiation, Closing). |
| **Dropdown (Multiple)** | Mark all products/services a client is interested in. |
| **Radio Select** | Capture yes/no style responses like “Is Budget Approved?”. |
| **Checkbox** | Flag if contracts or compliance documents are required. |
| **Date Picker** | Track key dates like follow-up or projected close date. |
| **File Upload** | Attach proposal files or client RFP documents. |
| **Signature** | Collect signed approvals directly within the opportunity. |

After selecting the appropriate field type, click **Next** to continue setting up the custom field.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155054375370/original/ZNUH2N7b69MRRigSqT6DyeW4Th65JVT_6Q.png?1758626138)

### **Assign to Opportunity**

After naming your field, set the **Object** to **Opportunity** so the field applies specifically within opportunity records. Once all details are filled in, click **Save** to create the new custom field.

**Other Fields**

- **Name:**The display label for the custom field (e.g., “Client Budget”).
- **Group:**Folder or category to organize the field under (e.g., “Budget Details”).
- **Placeholder:**A hint text shown inside the field when it’s empty (e.g., “Enter estimated value”).
- **Additional Preferences:**Advanced options for certain field types (e.g., default values, required toggle).

Click the **Save** button to finalize your new custom opportunity field. Once saved, the field becomes available for use across opportunity records in your pipeline.

```
Tip: If you mistakenly assign the field to Contact instead of Opportunity, it will only appear in contact records and won’t show in your pipeline opportunities.
```

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155054376449/original/j9cabOyyj4J9ACZ1y84ZRvvPHq5ZpQhTFQ.png?1758626669)

---

## **Creating a Folder**

Folders make it easy to organize multiple custom fields into logical groups. By creating folders, you can keep related fields together, reduce clutter, and make it simpler for your team to find and update the right information inside opportunities.

### **Add Folder**

Click the **Add Folder** button at the top right of the Custom Fields dashboard. Folders help you organize related fields, making them easier to manage and locate.

### 

### 

### **Name the Folder**

Enter a descriptive name for your folder (e.g., “Budget Details” or “Product Info”). A clear name ensures your team knows exactly what type of fields belong inside.

### 

### 

### **Select Object**

Choose **Opportunity** as the object so the folder applies specifically to opportunity records. This ensures all fields created under this folder appear in opportunities rather than contacts or other objects.

Click **Save**after finalizing the folder name and object.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155054379944/original/WAQBiC9X50g1rf85uERvXNw4SQKH5ykh0A.png?1758628211)

---

## **Managing Custom Fields**

Once your custom fields and folders are created, you can manage them effectively by reordering, filtering, grouping, or deleting. These tools help keep your opportunities organized and make it easier to find the right information.

### **Filter by Object**

Use the dropdown at the top right to filter custom fields by **object type** (e.g., Opportunity, Contact, Company). Selecting **Opportunity** ensures you only see fields linked to opportunities, making it easier to focus on what’s relevant for pipeline tracking.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155054382831/original/mzo5MU_Qeyfhb1GhjAbeM-bpV-sZwRQl0w.png?1758629521)

### **Group by Folder**

Use the **Group By** dropdown to organize custom fields by folder or category. This makes it easier to view fields based on context—for example, grouping all budget-related fields under “Opportunity Details” or all client inputs under a specific form.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155054383098/original/oJQwAGj8bvRdQfQ9kCSxC2ENRgcMt0GgCQ.png?1758629674)

### **Bulk Actions**

Select multiple custom fields using the checkbox menu and use the **Bulk Actions** menu to edit, delete, or move them into a different folder. This saves time when managing several fields at once instead of adjusting them individually.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155054383273/original/-z9GcnpsgtJtCXrGEjrSEXLq2UuRXytvGQ.png?1758629760)

**Reorder Fields**

Use the drag-and-drop **hamburger icon** to move custom fields up or down in the list. This allows you to control the order in which fields appear when creating or editing an opportunity.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155054379234/original/sU7SMNt7svHQQqdv0ccR0OSsu8UQBpz6Qg.gif?1758627952)

---

# **Using Custom Fields in Opportunities Dashboard**

Custom Fields are more than just data. they integrate into filtering, reporting, and pipeline views to make sales management easier.

### **Open Advanced Filters**

In the **Opportunities** view, click **Advanced Filters** to start applying custom filters to your pipeline. This opens the filtering panel where you can refine results using both standard fields and your custom opportunity fields.

### 

### 

### 

### **Filter by Custom Fields**

Inside the filtering panel, scroll down to the **Opportunities Custom Fields** section. This area displays all the opportunity custom fields you’ve created, both existing and newly added so you can filter records based on the data that matters most to your pipeline.

```
Tip: Combine multiple custom field filters to build precise views, such as identifying high-value leads that also meet specific qualification criteria.
```

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155054386717/original/3iXwCA98Td7yCvpET2QOGedWZuO55nO_ow.png?1758631026)

---

## **Display Custom Fields on Opportunity Cards**

Custom fields don’t just live inside the opportunity record, you can also make them visible on the pipeline cards. This ensures important details are available at a glance, helping your team work faster without opening each opportunity.

### **Open Manage Fields**

In the **Opportunities** view, click the **Manage Fields** button at the top right. This opens the customization panel, where you can adjust which details appear on opportunity cards.

For adding custom fields, simply scroll down to the **Add Fields** section.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155054389290/original/fwI06PtRXIIDKl8fHgZFCkUuHc5cAalezA.png?1758631844)

### **Add Custom Fields to Cards**

Expand the **Opportunity Details** section under **Add Fields** and check the custom fields you want to add. These fields will now appear directly on the card, giving you quick visibility into information like budgets, task types, or client preferences.

Once you’ve selected the custom fields you want, click the **Apply** button at the bottom of the panel. Your opportunity cards will instantly update to reflect the new field selections.

## 

### **Hide Empty Fields**

Inside any opportunity card, you’ll see the option to **Hide Empty Fields** at the top. Enabling this keeps your view clean by showing only fields with values, so you can focus on the information that actually matters.

This is especially helpful if you use many custom fields but only need to review the ones actively filled out for each opportunity.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155054394452/original/PoC7GGDak7xaSdGLx5TE-tJjSV59aE1SDw.png?1758634022)

---

# **Frequently Asked Questions**

**Q: If I add or remove custom fields from the Opportunity card using the “Manage Fields” option, will this change apply to all users in the account?**

No. Changes made in the **Manage Fields** panel apply only to your personal view of opportunity cards. Other users in the same sub-account will still see their own customized layouts unless they make adjustments themselves. This allows each user to display the fields most relevant to their role.

**Q: What happens to existing data if I delete an opportunity custom field?**

Deleting a custom field permanently removes the field and any data stored in it from all opportunities. This action cannot be undone. If you only want to hide a field without losing data, consider moving it into a folder or using the “Hide Empty Fields” option instead of deleting.

**Q: Can all custom field types be used for filtering opportunities?**

No. While most opportunity custom fields (such as dropdowns, numbers, dates, and text fields) can be used in filtering, certain field types like **File Upload** and **Signature** cannot be filtered. These fields still appear in opportunity records but won’t be available in the Advanced Filters panel.

**Q: How can I use opportunity custom fields in automations or workflows?**

Opportunity custom fields can be used as triggers, conditions, or actions in workflows. For example, you could:

- Update a custom field automatically (e.g., increase “Likelihood of Conversion” based on lead activity).
- Send personalized messages using merge fields that pull in opportunity custom field data.
- Create rules that move opportunities to a new stage when a custom field meets specific criteria.

  This integration ensures your custom data isn’t just stored—it actively drives automation in your pipeline.

---

## **Related Articles**

- ### [Customize Opportunity Cards in Board View](https://help.gohighlevel.com/a/solutions/articles/155000003910?portalId=48000045315)
- ### [Opportunities - FAQs](https://help.gohighlevel.com/a/solutions/articles/155000002000?portalId=48000045315)

title_en: Voice AI Agents Dashboard Overview
source_md:
The Voice AI Agents Dashboard helps you monitor call activity, agent performance, triggered actions, sentiment trends, and call logs from one place. Use the dashboard to understand how Voice AI agents are performing across inbound and outbound calls, compare performance over time, and review logs when you need more detail about specific calls or actions.

---

**TABLE OF CONTENTS**

- [What is the Voice AI Agents Dashboard?](#%E2%80%8B%E2%80%8BWhat-is-the-Voice-AI-Agents-Dashboard?)
- [Key Benefits of the Voice AI Agents Dashboard](#Key-Benefits-of-the-Voice-AI-Agents-Dashboard)
- [How To Access Dashboard & Logs](#How-To-Access-Dashboard-&-Logs)
- [Dashboard Views: Inbound and Outbound](#Dashboard-Views%3A-Inbound-and-Outbound)
- [Inbound Dashboard Metrics](#Inbound-Dashboard-Metrics)
- [Outbound Dashboard Metrics](#Outbound-Dashboard-Metrics)
- [Actions Triggered](#Actions-Triggered)
- [Sentiment Analysis](#Sentiment-Analysis)
- [Comparative Statistics and Percentage Changes](#Comparative-Statistics-and-Percentage-Changes)
- [Filters](#Filters)
- [Dashboard Metrics vs. Logs](#Dashboard-Metrics-vs.-Logs)
- [Live and Test Call Logs](#Live-and-Test-Call-Logs)
- [How To Use Dashboard Insights](#How-To-Use-Dashboard-Insights)
- [Frequently Asked Questions](#Frequently-Asked-Questions)
  - [Related Articles](#Related-Articles)

---

# **What is the Voice AI Agents Dashboard?**

The Voice AI Agents Dashboard provides performance insights for your Voice AI agents. It shows aggregate call metrics, action activity, sentiment trends, and logs so you can review how agents are handling conversations and identify areas that may need improvement.

Use the dashboard to monitor overall trends. Use logs when you need to investigate individual calls, test calls, triggered actions, or specific caller interactions.

---

## **Key Benefits of the Voice AI Agents Dashboard**

The dashboard gives your team a central place to review Voice AI performance and understand how callers are interacting with your agents. These insights can help you improve prompts, action setup, call routing, and follow-up processes.

- **Call performance visibility:** Review call volume, completion trends, duration, and call outcomes.

- **Inbound and outbound reporting:** Switch between inbound and outbound views to understand different call types.

- **Action tracking:** See how often configured actions are triggered during calls.

- **Sentiment insights:** Review caller sentiment trends to identify positive, neutral, or negative patterns.

- **Agent comparison:** Filter by agent to compare performance across different Voice AI agents.

- **Call-level investigation:** Use logs to review specific live or test calls after identifying a trend.

---

## **How To Access Dashboard & Logs**

Dashboard & Logs is available from the Voice AI area inside AI Agents. This page lets you move between the agent list and dashboard reporting so you can review performance without opening each agent individually.

1. Go to **AI Agents**.
2. Select **Voice AI**.
3. Click **Dashboard & Logs**.
4. Use the dashboard filters to choose the call type, agent, and date range you want to review.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155073522823/original/2KxaTEqhVuX38Jx7OyOJ0ovOorMHfqQxZA.png?1781249508)

---

## **Dashboard Views: Inbound and Outbound**

The dashboard includes separate views for inbound and outbound Voice AI activity. These views help you review the metrics that matter most for each call direction.

**Inbound** focuses on calls received by Voice AI agents. This view helps you understand how agents are handling incoming caller conversations, actions, and sentiment.

**Outbound** focuses on calls placed by Voice AI agents. This view helps you understand outbound call outcomes, such as whether calls were answered, went to voicemail, were not answered, or failed.

**![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155073523004/original/Tb8sMtiu4m_G8meUosgWov6taKZzV47JAA.gif?1781249634)**

---

## **Inbound Dashboard Metrics**

Inbound dashboard metrics show how Voice AI agents are handling incoming calls. These metrics help you understand call volume, engagement, actions completed, and caller experience.

Common inbound metrics may include:

- **Total Calls:** The number of inbound calls handled during the selected time period.

- **Actions Triggered:** The number of configured actions triggered during calls.

- **Sentiment:** AI-analyzed caller sentiment across calls.

- **Calls Completed:** A trend chart showing completed call activity over time.

- **Total Duration:** The total amount of call time for the selected period.

- **Average Call Duration:** The average length of completed calls.

- **SMS Sent:** The number of SMS actions sent by Voice AI.

- **Workflows Triggered:** The number of workflows triggered during calls.

- **Call Transfers:** The number of calls transferred.

- **Custom Actions:** The number of configured custom actions triggered.

- **Appointment Booking:** The number of appointment booking actions completed or attempted.

- **Contact Info Updated:** The number of times contact information was updated.

A sudden increase or decrease in these metrics may be caused by changes in call volume, campaigns, agent configuration, prompts, or action setup.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155073539047/original/eUvCYusKQXTGnoTPAv8SvALHqZvUq0Q_VA.png?1781260337)

---

## **Outbound Dashboard Metrics**

Outbound dashboard metrics help you review the results of calls placed by Voice AI agents. These metrics are useful for understanding connection rates and outbound call outcomes.

Common outbound metrics may include:

- **Human Answered:** Calls answered by a person.

- **Voicemail:** Calls that reached voicemail.

- **No Answer:** Calls that were not answered.

- **Failed:** Calls that could not be completed.

- **Attempted Calls:** A log or count of outbound call attempts.

Use outbound metrics to evaluate whether outbound campaigns are reaching contacts successfully and whether call outcomes align with expectations.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155073537646/original/zSTtjYb5Cq7x4Juc_DLVI5V0UK_qFlTKhQ.png?1781259781)

---

## **Actions Triggered**

Actions Triggered shows how often Voice AI agents completed configured actions during calls. These metrics depend on the actions configured for the selected agent and the call scenarios that occurred during the selected time period.

Actions may include:

- Call Transfer

- Send SMS

- Trigger a Workflow

- Custom Action

- Appointment Booking

- Cancel Appointment

- Reschedule Appointment

- Contact Info Updated

Use this data to confirm whether agents are completing the expected outcomes. For example, if an agent is designed to book appointments but Appointment Booking activity is low, review the prompt, booking setup, calendar availability, and call logs.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155073537492/original/irJHM_Ffu3VMN8DRBv4Ty6c62PsAPpN2ew.png?1781259694)

---

## **Sentiment Analysis**

Sentiment Analysis groups calls into positive, neutral, or negative trends based on AI interpretation of caller experience. This can help you identify patterns in how callers respond to Voice AI interactions.

Use sentiment as a directional signal, not as a perfect customer satisfaction score. For full context, review call logs, transcripts, recordings, and call outcomes.

Examples of how to use sentiment:

- Review negative sentiment calls to identify confusing prompts or failed handoffs.

- Compare sentiment across agents to find agents that may need prompt or action updates.

- Look for sentiment changes after updating prompts, knowledge sources, or call routing.

---

## **Comparative Statistics and Percentage Changes**

Some dashboard cards may show percentage changes compared with a previous reporting period. This helps you understand whether a metric is increasing or decreasing over time.

Percentage delta compares the selected reporting period with the previous equivalent period. For example, if you filter the dashboard to the last 7 days, the comparison reflects the previous 7-day period.

Review changes in context. A metric may increase or decrease because of:

- Higher or lower call volume

- New or paused campaigns

- Prompt changes

- Agent setting updates

- Calendar or workflow changes

- Seasonal call patterns

- Changes in inbound or outbound traffic

---

## **Filters**

Filters help you narrow dashboard results so you can review the right agent, call direction, timeframe, or call activity. Applying filters changes the metrics and logs shown on the page.

Common filters may include:

- **Inbound / Outbound:** Switch between inbound and outbound call reporting.

- **Agent:** View data for all agents or a specific Voice AI agent.

- **Date Range:** Review performance for a selected time period.

- **Live / Test:** Filter logs by live calls, test calls, or both.

- **Contact Name:** Search logs for a specific contact.

- **Action Type:** Filter logs by actions such as Call Transfer, Send SMS, Trigger a Workflow, Custom Action, Appointment Booking, Cancel Appointment, or Reschedule Appointment.

If metrics look lower or higher than expected, check the selected filters first.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155073539810/original/mWfYfv830GtI6gF6BhD3HzO2_4fGiR9_VA.gif?1781260499)

---

## **Dashboard Metrics vs. Logs**

Dashboard metrics and logs work together, but they serve different purposes. The dashboard gives you aggregate performance trends, while logs help you review specific calls and actions.

| **Area** | **Use It For** | **Example** |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Dashboard Metrics** | Reviewing trends and totals across selected agents or time periods | Total calls, average duration, sentiment, actions triggered |
| **Logs** | Investigating individual calls or actions | Call details, test calls, contact-specific activity, action history |
| **Agent Logs** | Reviewing deeper call execution details | Execution timeline, transfers, latency, failures, and debugging context |

Use the dashboard to find patterns. Use logs when you need to understand what happened during a specific call.

---

## **Live and Test Call Logs**

The logs area can help you review both live and test call activity. This is useful when you want to validate agent behavior before launch or investigate a specific call after it happens.

Test calls may appear in dashboard logs when filtered by call type, but test calls are excluded from dashboard analytics and performance metrics. This means a test call can appear in logs without increasing dashboard totals such as Total Calls or Actions Triggered.

Use the **Live / Test** filter to separate live customer calls from test calls.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155073539947/original/jJOC7JDQhIP9Gs4T0d2VQ9PjNZujNEtA7A.png?1781260589)

---

## **How To Use Dashboard Insights**

Dashboard insights are most useful when you connect the numbers to specific follow-up actions. Use the dashboard to identify trends, then review logs or agent settings to understand what may need improvement.

Examples:

- **High call volume with low action completion:** Review whether the agent prompt clearly guides callers toward the intended action.

- **Long average call duration:** Review transcripts to see whether callers are confused, asking complex questions, or being routed inefficiently.

- **Negative sentiment trend:** Review call recordings or transcripts to identify frustrating moments in the conversation.

- **Low workflow trigger count:** Confirm the workflow action is configured and that the agent has clear instructions for when to trigger it.

- **Low appointment booking activity:** Review calendar availability, booking setup, prompt instructions, and appointment-related logs.

- **Agent performance differences:** Filter by agent to compare results and identify which agents may need prompt, action, or knowledge updates.

---

## **Frequently Asked Questions**

**Q: What does the Voice AI Agents Dashboard show?**  
It shows Voice AI performance data such as call activity, duration, triggered actions, sentiment trends, filters, and logs.

**Q: What is the difference between dashboard analytics and logs?**  
Dashboard analytics show aggregate performance trends. Logs show individual call or action records that can be reviewed in more detail.

**Q: Are test calls included in dashboard analytics?**  
No. Test calls may appear in logs, but they are excluded from dashboard analytics and performance metrics.

**Q: Can I filter the dashboard by agent?**  
Yes. Use the agent filter to review all agents or a specific Voice AI agent.

**Q: What does percentage delta mean?**  
Percentage delta compares the selected reporting period with the previous equivalent period.

**Q: What does sentiment analysis measure?**  
Sentiment analysis uses AI to estimate whether caller experience appears positive, neutral, or negative. Review logs or recordings for full context.

**Q: Why is my dashboard empty?**  
The selected filters may not include any live call activity, or the agent may not have completed calls during the selected date range.

**Q: Why are action counts different from workflow activity?**  
Dashboard action counts reflect Voice AI actions triggered during calls. Workflow activity may have its own execution records and filters.

**Q: When should I use Agent Logs instead of the dashboard?**  
Use Agent Logs when you need call-level details such as execution timeline, transfers, latency, failures, or debugging context.

**Q: Can I review outbound-specific performance?**  
Yes. Use the Outbound dashboard view to review outbound outcomes such as Human Answered, Voicemail, No Answer, Failed, and attempted calls.

---

### **Related Articles**

- [Testing Voice AI Agents in HighLevel: Calls and Logs](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000004108-testing-voice-ai-agents)

- [Test Call Logs visible in Voice AI Dashboard](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000005211-test-call-logs-visible-in-voice-ai-dashboard)

- [Voice AI - Agent Logs](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000007687-voice-ai-agent-logs)

- [Call Logs for Voice AI Agents](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000005900-call-logs-for-voice-ai-agents)

- [Voice AI Performance Reports](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000007984-voice-ai-performance-reports)

- [Voice AI Outbound Calling Dashboard](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000006680-voice-ai-outbound-calling-dashboard)

Inline Forms and Surveys let you collect quick feedback directly from an email campaign using rating, scoring, and sentiment-based response options. When a recipient selects an option, HighLevel records the response in the campaign's submission data, and you can optionally redirect the recipient to a Success URL afterward. This makes the element useful for satisfaction surveys, NPS-style feedback, content ratings, and other lightweight feedback requests.

---

- [Reviewing Inline Feedback Submissions](#Reviewing-Inline-Feedback-Submissions)
