4. **Review the amount applied.**  
     
   Confirm the Gift Card amount before proceeding.

   - If the Gift Card covers the full amount, no additional payment method is charged for that payment.
   - If the Gift Card does not cover the full amount, the available Gift Card balance is applied first.  
       
     ![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155079733223/original/sZJ0OLrbZgH8AVHOPPzHfkslGxCvPVdHhQ.png?1788196629)
5. **Add or select a payment method when a balance remains.**  
     
   If there is still an amount due after applying the Gift Card, you can use a saved card or add a new card to collect the remaining balance.  
     
   ![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155079733307/original/0g2nUW_zuaptsg2cYcjffWgki3Cer1xY7w.png?1788196673)
6. **Complete the payment.**  
     
   Review the final payment summary and submit the payment.
7. **Verify the completed redemption.**  
     
   After a successful payment:

   - Open **Transaction Details** to confirm the Gift Card amount used.
   - Review the associated **Gift Card Order** to confirm its updated remaining balance.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155079733352/original/FRKtFTbvOZD0FN2xp9Er2AMYcSfKv7KtlQ.png?1788196708)

---

## **Frequently Asked Questions**

**Q: Can I apply more than one Gift Card to the same payment?**  
No. You can apply one Gift Card per payment.

**Q: Can a Test Mode Gift Card be used for a Live Mode payment?**  
No. Gift Cards purchased in Test Mode can only be redeemed in Test Mode, while Gift Cards purchased in Live Mode can only be redeemed in Live Mode.

**Q: Can I redeem a Gift Card that I sent directly to a customer without collecting payment for it?**  
Yes. You can redeem a Gift Card that was sent directly to a customer as long as it is active, has not expired, and has an available balance.

**Q: What if the customer does not already have a saved card and the Gift Card does not cover the full payment?**  
You can add a new card to collect the remaining amount.

**Q: Is there a dedicated user permission specifically for redeeming Gift Cards?**  
No dedicated Gift Card redemption permission is currently available. Users still need appropriate access to the payment area where the Gift Card is being redeemed.

---

## **Related Articles**

- [Getting Started with Gift Cards](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000006980?utm_source=chatgpt.com)
- [How to Sell Gift Cards](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000006986?utm_source=chatgpt.com)
- [How to Send Gift Cards](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000006987?utm_source=chatgpt.com)
- [How to Track Gift Card Performance (Analytics & Metric Tracking)](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000006981-how-to-track-gift-card-performance-analytics-metric-tracking-?utm_source=chatgpt.com)
- [Create Subscriptions and Invoices in Contact Details Page](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000004064-create-or-schedule-subscriptions-and-send-invoice-within-contact-details-page?utm_source=chatgpt.com)
- [How to add and manage your customer's cards on file](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000004506-how-to-add-and-manage-your-customer-s-cards-on-file?utm_source=chatgpt.com)

title_en: Social Planner - Advanced CSV for Bulk Scheduling
source_md:
Schedule multiple social media posts at once using Advanced CSV Bulk Scheduling in HighLevel Social Planner. Upload a CSV or XLSX file to organize posts, media, publishing dates, and platform-specific settings.

This guide explains how to prepare your file, import posts, and resolve common scheduling errors.

```
Please Note: Refer to Prerequisite for Bulk CSV - Basic and Advance CSV article for CSV Upload options for bulk scheduling.
```

---

**TABLE OF CONTENTS**

- [What is Advanced CSV for Bulk Scheduling in Social Planner?](#What-is-Advanced-CSV-for-Bulk-Scheduling-in-Social-Planner?)
- [Key Benefits of Advanced CSV for Bulk Scheduling](#Key-Benefits-of-Advanced-CSV-for-Bulk-Scheduling)
- [Before You Begin](#Before-You-Begin)
- [How To Use Advanced CSV for Bulk Scheduling](#How-To-Use-Advanced-CSV-for-Bulk-Scheduling)
- [Media Support by Platform (Images, Reels, and Videos)](#Media-Support-by-Platform-(Images,-Reels,-and-Videos))
- [Image Support](#Image-Support)
- [Reel and Video Support](#Reel-and-Video-Support)
- [Uploading or Updating Images After CSV Import](#Uploading-or-Updating-Images-After-CSV-Import)
- [Watermark Support](#Watermark-Support)
- [Smart Media Optimization](#Smart-Media-Optimization)
- [Tag & Category Assignment](#Tag-&-Category-Assignment)
- [Flexible Date-Time Parsing](#Flexible-Date-Time-Parsing)
- [Advanced CSV Features and Media Support](#Advanced-CSV-Features-and-Media-Support)
- [Frequently Asked Questions](#Frequently-Asked-Questions)
- [Related Articles](#Related-Articles)

---

## **What is Advanced CSV for Bulk Scheduling in Social Planner?**

Advanced CSV Bulk Scheduling allows you to create and schedule multiple social media posts from a single spreadsheet. Compared with the Basic CSV format, Advanced CSV supports additional options such as platform-specific post types, video thumbnails, watermarks, tags, categories, and approval workflows.

---

## **Key Benefits of Advanced CSV for Bulk Scheduling**

Unlocking the Advanced CSV feature brings a host of advantages designed to simplify and supercharge your social media scheduling:

 

- **Bulk Scheduling Across Platforms:** Schedule posts, stories, reels, shorts, and more for multiple channels in one upload.
- **Watermark Automation:** Automatically brand your media with watermarks for consistent visual identity.
- **Smart Media Optimization:** Ensure images and videos are auto-optimized for each platform’s requirements.
- **Tag & Category Assignment:** Organize posts with tags and categories for streamlined reporting and automation triggers.
- **Flexible Date-Time Parsing:** Supports multiple date-time formats, reducing import errors and saving time.
- **Dual Format Upload:** Accepts both .csv and .xlsx files, removing friction during import.
- **Performance Upgrades:** Experience faster workflows, smoother imports, and improved error handling.
- **First-Time Comments & Follow-Ups:** Add initial comments to posts for higher engagement.
- **Comprehensive Platform Support:** Configure Google Business Profile, YouTube, TikTok, and more with platform-specific fields.

---

## **Before You Begin**

Preparing the Advanced CSV template correctly helps prevent import errors and ensures posts are scheduled as intended.

- **Connect Social Accounts:** Make sure the accounts you want to publish to are connected in **Marketing → Social Planner**.
- **Download the Template:** Use the current Advanced CSV template to preserve the required column names.
- **Prepare Media URLs:** Upload media to the HighLevel Media Library and use accessible URLs. Google Drive links are not supported for CSV media imports.
- **Format Scheduling Dates:** Use a supported 24-hour date/time format, such as `2026-11-10 14:30`.
- **Allow Scheduling Time:** Set publishing times at least 10 minutes after the expected import time.
- **Check Platform Requirements:** Confirm that your captions and media meet the restrictions of each selected social platform.

---

## **How To Use Advanced CSV for Bulk Scheduling**

The Advanced CSV importer lets you upload your content, select publishing destinations, review errors, and schedule multiple posts in one workflow.

 

### **Step 1:**Navigate to Social Planner

1. Go to **Marketing**from your account.
2. Click on the **Social****Planner** tab.
3. Connect your preferred social accounts.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155085058138/original/VHMOGfrUQc0iaVwoPBdhBW7jQ9nFLftgsg.png?1793892082)

### **Step 2:**Start a New Bulk Upload

1. Click on the **+ New Post**button.
2. Select the **Upload from CSV** option from the drop-down.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155085058309/original/KohZpiBywOnrDXUdWnInflufryBLIENt7g.gif?1793892150)

### **Step 3:**Upload CSV File

1. Select **Advance Format** to unlock all enhanced features.
2. **Upload** your filled-out .csv or .xlsx file.
3. Click on **Next**.

```
Note: Download Advanced and Basic CSV Template sample here. The latest templates include a thumbnailUrl column for video thumbnails.
Note: Download Advanced and Basic CSV template samples here.
```

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155085058337/original/3eFz9E_76cmetiNgMeDZKwWxyQqYe6LJ6w.png?1793892181)

### **Step 4:**Select Social Accounts & Approval Settings

1. Select social **Channel/Channels** you want to post to.
2. If the posts need approval, click on the **Send for approval** box to turn it on and **select an approver**.
3. Click on **Create**.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155085058456/original/gfoW-i1DP5BP1aQuEtxL7KMj_MHnn2O3Ew.png?1793892233)

### **Step 5:** Review & Correct Errors

1. The system will flag any issues.
2. **Review** and **correct** them before proceeding.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155085058586/original/TfZIdvR7_eXjANKe-vK50myC0tvAzDQhrA.png?1793892299)

### **Step 6:** Schedule and Import

1. Click on **Schedule**.
2. Click on **Import** to add all approved posts to your calendar queue.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155085058630/original/D6vbEsUsAtH3_3BjMH7h6_Qhbbgvb17dEw.png?1793892327)

---

## **Media Support by Platform (Images, Reels, and Videos)**

When using **Advanced CSV for Bulk Scheduling**, you can schedule posts across multiple social media platforms such as **Facebook, Instagram, Google My Business, LinkedIn,**and many more. Media support varies by platform, so it’s important to follow the guidelines below to ensure posts are scheduled successfully.

A sample of this spreadsheet can be found here as stated in the screenshot below:-

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155064584491/original/_VllGVchUAOJG1fnH-tDe2MsSpYZozTnmw.png?1770727501)

---

## **Image Support**

### **1. Facebook and Instagram**

- Support **image carousels**
- You can add **multiple image URLs** in the spreadsheet
- Multiple image URLs must be **comma-separated**
- Example:  
    
  ![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155064585354/original/9TjQqhcUi-aGV54J7MYjvT3lueC6sutfJQ.png?1770728035)

### **2. Google My Business**

- Supports **only one image per post**
- Image carousels are **not supported**

---

## **Reel and Video Support**

- Only **one video or reel** is supported per post
- Carousels are **not supported** for reels or videos
- If multiple video URLs are added, the post may fail to schedule
- You can set a custom thumbnail for video posts using the thumbnailUrl field in your CSV/XLSX file.
- The thumbnail is automatically applied to the first video in the post.
- Multiple video thumbnails are not supported, and behavior may vary across social platforms.  
    
    
  ![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155064585853/original/1ejmO7onesMJtKRGRvP5o7GBBGNvasg8zg.png?1770728323)

---

## **Uploading or Updating Images After CSV Import**

In addition to adding media URLs in the spreadsheet, you can also upload or modify images during the scheduling flow:

On the **3rd review screen**, you can:

- Add new images
- Update existing images
- Upload additional images (where supported by the platform)

This method can be used if you prefer not to include all media URLs directly in the CSV file.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155064588185/original/tzY2qCi_8-7l11PaomurmgA8KRXBGGZ6IQ.png?1770729551)

```
IMPORTANT: If you select Facebook (which supports multiple images in a carousel) and GMB (which supports only 1 image per feed), the first image selected would be posted on GMB and all the images on Facebook.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155064587871/original/yZmKPX58TX5s9bTJOGnTyDkiQ0YSxiAdzA.png?1770729393)
```

---

## **Watermark Support**

Automatically apply watermarks to your images and videos by specifying watermark fields in your CSV. This ensures consistent branding across all posts without manual editing.

 

- Add watermark file paths or settings in the designated CSV columns.
- Watermarks are applied during the import process for all supported platforms.

---

## **Smart Media Optimization**

Media files are auto-optimized for each platform’s requirements, ensuring your content looks its best and meets technical specifications.

- Images and videos are resized, compressed, or reformatted as needed.
- Platform-specific media settings can be configured in the CSV template.

---

## **Tag & Category Assignment**

Assign tags and categories to each post directly in your CSV to streamline reporting, automation, and organization.

 

- Use the relevant columns in the template to add multiple tags or categories.
- Note: Tags and categories will not transfer when importing from a snapshot or template into a new location.

## 

## **Flexible Date-Time Parsing**

Reduce import errors by using any of the supported date-time formats in your CSV. The system will recognize and process a wide range of common formats, including:

 

- YYYY-MM-DD HH:mm
- YYYY-MM-DD HH:mm:ss
- YYYY/MM/DD HH:mm:ss
- YYYY/MM/DD HH:mm
- MM/DD/YYYY H:mm:ss
- MM-DD-YYYY H:mm:ss
- MM/DD/YYYY H:mm
- MM-DD-YYYY H:mm

---

## **Advanced CSV Features and Media Support**

The Advanced CSV template includes additional fields for customizing posts across supported social platforms.

Available settings and media limits depend on the selected platform and post type.

| Feature | Description |
| --- | --- |
| **Post Types** | Configure supported feed posts, Stories, Reels, and Shorts. |
| **Images** | Add image URLs, including multiple images where carousels are supported. |
| **Video Thumbnails** | Use `thumbnailUrl` for a supported video post. The thumbnail applies to the first video. |
| **Media Optimization** | Use `mediaOptimization` to request supported media adjustments. |
| **Watermarks** | Use `applyWatermark` to apply the configured watermark to supported image posts. |
| **Tags and Categories** | Organize imported posts with the relevant template columns. |
| **Follow-Up Comments** | Add a first comment on supported platforms. |
| **Platform Settings** | Configure available options for Google Business Profile, YouTube, TikTok, Pinterest, and other supported channels. |

**Important:** Media optimization does not guarantee that every unsupported file or post format can be published. Review platform requirements before importing.

---

## **Frequently Asked Questions**

**Q: Can I use both .csv and .xlsx files for bulk scheduling?**

Yes, both file formats are supported for Advanced CSV uploads.

**Q: Why can't I use Google Drive links in my CSV imports anymore?**

Due to recent changes by Google, we can no longer process Google Drive links during CSV imports. 

To ensure smooth uploads, please upload your media files directly to the Media Library and use those 

Media Library links in your CSV file instead.

**Q: What is the number of posts allowed via CSV at one time?**

The number of posts allowed in CSV is 90 posts per CSV. You will need to divide that across all the Social outlets you are posting out to.

**Q: Can I import tags and category to new location via snapshot?**

When importing CSV from a snapshot or template, tags and categories will not transfer to a new location.

**Q: What happens if my CSV contains errors or invalid data?**

The system will flag errors during the review step. You must correct these before importing.

**Q: Are watermarks applied to all media types?**

Watermarks are applied to supported image and video formats as specified in the CSV.

**Q: Will tags and categories transfer if I import a CSV from a snapshot or template?**

No, tags and categories do not transfer when importing from a snapshot or template into a new location.

**Q: Can I schedule posts for all supported platforms in one CSV upload?**

Yes, you can schedule posts for multiple platforms, including Stories, Reels, Shorts, Google Business Profile, TikTok, Pinterest, and more.

**Q: How do I specify a Pinterest board in the CSV?**

This is not supported as of now.

**Q: What if I need to add a first-time comment to a post?**

Include your comment in the relevant field in the Advanced CSV template.

**Q: Is there a limit to the number of posts I can schedule in one upload?**

There is no strict limit, but extremely large files may take longer to process.

---

## **Related Articles**

1. [Getting Started - Setup Social Planner](https://help.gohighlevel.com/en/support/solutions/articles/155000005063)
2. [Prerequisite for Bulk CSV - Basic and Advance CSV](https://help.gohighlevel.com/en/support/solutions/articles/155000005411)
3. [Social Planner: In-App Notification Banner for Disconnected Accounts](https://help.gohighlevel.com/en/support/solutions/articles/155000005535)
4. [How to post Recurring Social Posts through the Social Planner?](https://help.gohighlevel.com/en/support/solutions/articles/155000000648)

title_en: How to Use Workflow Maps in HighLevel
source_md:
Workflow Maps in HighLevel provides a visual overview of your workflows, folders, and connected assets. It helps you understand how automations work together without opening each workflow individually. You can explore dependencies, trace Contact Journeys, review errors, and identify opportunities to organize your account. This article explains how to navigate Workflow Maps and use its main features.

---

**TABLE OF CONTENTS**

- [What is Workflow Maps?](#What-is-Workflow-Maps?)
- [Key Benefits of Workflow Maps](#Key-Benefits-of-Workflow-Maps)
- [How to Use Workflow Maps](#How-to-Use-Workflow-Maps)
- [Understanding the Workflow Map](#Understanding-the-Workflow-Map)
- [Searching and Navigating Workflow Maps](#Searching-and-Navigating-Workflow-Maps)
- [Exploring Connected Workflows and Assets](#Exploring-Connected-Workflows-and-Assets)
- [Tracing Contact Journeys](#Tracing-Contact-Journeys)
- [Troubleshooting Workflow Errors](#Troubleshooting-Workflow-Errors)
- [Organizing the Map and Using Cleanup](#Organizing-the-Map-and-Using-Cleanup)
- [AI Assistant, Onboarding, and Resources](#AI-Assistant,-Onboarding,-and-Resources)
- [Frequently Asked Questions](#Frequently-Asked-Questions)
- [Related Articles](#Related-Articles)

---

# **What is Workflow Maps?**

Workflow Maps is a visual workspace that displays your existing workflows and their connections to supported assets, including tags, forms, calendars, pipelines, and custom fields.

For example, a form submission may start one workflow, which adds a tag that triggers another workflow. Workflow

Maps helps you see these relationships and understand the larger automation process.

Maps are generated from your existing workflows, so you do not need to create diagrams manually. Each sub-account has its own map.

**Availability:** At launch, Workflow Maps is available to **agency users and agency admins**. The release demonstration also references Labs availability. Confirm whether Labs activation is required for your account.

---

## **Key Benefits of Workflow Maps**

Workflow Maps helps you investigate automation relationships and maintain a more organized account.

- **Visual Overview:** See workflows, folders, and connected assets together.
- **Dependency Tracking:** Identify which workflows use specific assets.
- **Quick Navigation:** Search, filter, and explore workflows from one workspace.
- **Contact Journey Tracking:** Review a Contact's workflow enrollment history.
- **Error Investigation:** Find workflows with failed executions and inspect available details.
- **Account Organization:** Review folders, layouts, and potential cleanup opportunities.
- **AI Assistance:** Get help understanding your automations through the available assistant.

---

## **How to Use Workflow Maps**

Workflow Maps is useful when reviewing an unfamiliar account, investigating a Contact's experience, or checking dependencies before changing an automation.

### 

### **Step 1: Open Workflow Maps**

1. Open the relevant HighLevel sub-account.
2. Go to **Automation → Workflows**.
3. Select **Workflow Maps**.

You can also open **Maps** from a workflow's builder.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155084426944/original/S2DEsxilztDm3JqrEU5uykA0hRmDKpnGkQ.png?1793199612)

### 

### **Step 2: Explore Your Workflows**

1. Review the workflows and folders shown on the map.
2. Use **Fit** to display the complete view.
3. Select a workflow or asset.
4. Review its available details and connections.

### 

### **Step 3: Find Specific Workflows or Assets**

1. Open **Search**.
2. Enter the name of a workflow, asset, trigger, or action.
3. Select a result.
4. Apply filters to narrow the view if needed.

### **Step 4: Review Connections**

1. Select the workflow or asset you want to investigate.
2. Review its connected items.
3. Open **Linked workflows** when available to explore related workflows together.
4. Open the relevant workflow in Workflow Builder if changes are required.

### **Step 5: Investigate a Contact Journey**

1. Open the Contact tracing interface.
2. Search for and select the Contact.
3. Review their available enrollment history.
4. Inspect relevant waiting, completed, or failed activity.

### **Step 6: Review Errors and Cleanup Findings**

1. Use the available error filters or review interface to find workflows requiring attention.
2. Inspect the affected execution.
3. Open Workflow Builder if the workflow needs correction.
4. Review Cleanup findings when available to identify organization opportunities.

### **Step 7: Get Additional Help**

1. Open the Workflow Maps AI assistant if available.
2. Ask a question about the workflows or assets you are investigating.
3. Use onboarding or Resources for additional guidance.

```
Tip: Review connected workflows before modifying important assets so you can identify potential dependencies.
```

---

## **Understanding the Workflow Map**

The map displays workflows within folders and shows their relationships with supported assets. Understanding these elements helps you identify automation dependencies before making changes.

| Element | Description |
| --- | --- |
| Workflow | An automation in your sub-account |
| Folder | A group of related workflows |
| Asset | A connected tag, form, calendar, pipeline, custom field, or other supported item |
| Connection | A relationship involving a workflow or asset |
| Sticky Note | An annotation used to document the map |

Select a workflow or asset to explore its available details and connections.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155084428102/original/hxFafz_ufzTQ7gJZ8ncCwNAjoGUjgWuBdQ.png?1793200169)

```
Note: Workflow Maps shows how automations are configured. It does not mean that a particular Contact has completed every visible connection.
```

For additional details, see [Read the map and understand connections](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000009460-read-the-map-and-understand-connections).

---

## **Searching and Navigating Workflow Maps**

Search and navigation controls help you locate specific workflows or assets and focus on the connections that matter.

Available controls include:

- **Search:** Find workflows, assets, triggers, and actions by name.
- **Filters:** Narrow the visible map using supported criteria.
- **Pan and Zoom:** Move around the map and inspect details.
- **Fit:** Adjust the view to display the full map.
- **2D/3D:** Switch between available viewing modes.

You can also refresh map data when you need to review updated workflow information.

```
Tip: If a workflow or asset is missing, check the active filters and refresh the map before continuing.
```

For detailed instructions, see [Navigate, search, and filter Workflow Maps](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000009461-navigate-search-and-filter-workflow-maps).

---

## **Exploring Connected Workflows and Assets**

Connected workflows and assets help you understand how one automation may affect another.

Selecting an asset reveals its available workflow relationships. For example, you can investigate which workflows use a particular tag before changing that tag.

### **Linked Workflows and Workflow View**

The **Linked workflows** option lets you explore related workflows together in a focused view.

Existing documentation refers to this interface as **Workflow view**, while the release also uses the term *Workflow Canvas*. Follow the labels shown in your HighLevel interface.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155084430958/original/Sy9D3MeVV8S_EyQvz4YDDcZnY1D5IIY0-w.png?1793201510)

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155084431821/original/vh9HuhicxG6GQdUh2dcmSISKpu0EWH2cQA.png?1793201893)

```
Important: Workflow Maps helps you investigate connections. To edit workflow triggers, actions, or internal logic, open the workflow in Workflow Builder.
```

---

## **Tracing Contact Journeys**

Contact Journeys helps you understand how an individual Contact has progressed through multiple workflows.

You can search for a Contact and review available enrollment history, including completed activities, waiting steps, and failed executions.

The existing HighLevel documentation describes a **60-day history window** for Contact tracing.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155084432092/original/Szm2_lUgKeJ3fCCBR6SKX1fXw8C46cr-hw.png?1793202048)

```
Tip: Use Contact Journeys to investigate what happened to a particular Contact. Use the main map to understand how workflows are connected.
```

For detailed instructions, see [Trace a contact through workflows](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000009465-trace-a-contact-through-workflows).

---

## **Troubleshooting Workflow Errors**

Workflow Maps helps you locate automations with execution problems and inspect the affected steps.

You can review available error indicators, investigate failed executions, and open the relevant workflow for further troubleshooting.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155084432283/original/mi17RZl-2RKH3NmJAD_dky_6ShrOVKOjJw.png?1793202172)

```
Important: Selecting Mark as read clears an error notification badge. It does not repair the workflow or retry the failed execution.
```

For additional guidance, see [Review workflows with errors](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000009464-review-workflows-with-errors).

---

## **Organizing the Map and Using Cleanup**

Workflow Maps includes organization tools that can help keep complex automation environments easier to understand.

### **Organizing Folders and Layouts**

Agency admins can organize supported workflows and folders, adjust their arrangement, and save shared map layouts.

Saved organizational changes can affect other users who access the same sub-account.

```
Note: Access to view Workflow Maps does not necessarily include permission to modify or save its shared layout.
```

### **Cleanup**

The release describes Cleanup as a way to identify possible maintenance tasks, including:

- Workflows with default names.
- Workflows without recent enrollments.
- Empty folders.

These findings can help you decide which items need attention.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155084432606/original/pEEL63lbL8okp3izDqUuYyScAWwrausHVw.png?1793202313)

```
Important: Cleanup criteria, permissions, and management actions require confirmation. Do not assume that Cleanup automatically deletes or fixes anything.
```

---

## **AI Assistant, Onboarding, and Resources**

Workflow Maps includes guidance features to help users understand the map and investigate their automation environment.

### **AI Assistant**

The release describes an AI assistant that can help answer questions about workflow connections, troubleshooting, and account organization.

For example, you may ask which workflows are connected to a particular asset.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155084432944/original/pEeT0QRNfwcjfTc-UoFW_KdI9u-kW1gfjA.png?1793202483)

```
Note: The assistant's exact capabilities require verification. Do not assume it can edit workflows or resolve errors automatically.
```

### **Onboarding and Resources**

Guided onboarding and Resources help users learn the interface and access available walkthroughs or reference material.

The exact controls and content may vary according to feature availability.

---

## **Frequently Asked Questions**

**Q: Do I need to create Workflow Maps manually?**

A: No. HighLevel generates maps from the existing workflows and supported asset connections in your sub-account.

**Q: Who can access Workflow Maps?**

A: The release specifies agency users and agency admins at launch. Exact eligibility and any Labs requirements should be confirmed.

**Q: Can I edit workflow steps directly from Workflow Maps?**

A: No. Open the workflow in Workflow Builder to edit its triggers, actions, or internal logic.

**Q: Can Workflow Maps show a Contact's complete history?**

A: Contact tracing displays the available workflow history. The existing documentation describes a 60-day history window.

**Q: What should I do if a workflow is missing from the map?**

A: Check your filters, search for the workflow, and refresh the map data.

**Q: Does marking a workflow error as read fix it?**

A: No. Mark as read clears the notification badge. The underlying error still requires investigation.

**Q: Can everyone change the map layout?**

A: No. The existing documentation identifies agency-admin permissions for organizing and saving shared layouts.

**Q: Does Cleanup automatically remove unused workflows?**

A: The release describes Cleanup as a way to identify items requiring review. Automatic deletion or repair is not confirmed.

**Q: Can the AI assistant modify my workflows?**

A: The release describes assistance with understanding and troubleshooting automations. Workflow-editing capabilities require separate verification.

---

### **Related Articles**

- [Read the map and understand connections](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000009460-read-the-map-and-understand-connections)
- [Navigate, search, and filter Workflow Maps](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000009461-navigate-search-and-filter-workflow-maps)
- [Find where an asset is used](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000009462-find-where-an-asset-is-used)
- [Follow linked workflows](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000009463-follow-linked-workflows)
- [Review workflows with errors](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000009464-review-workflows-with-errors)
- [Trace a contact through workflows](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000009465-trace-a-contact-through-workflows)

title_en: Workflow Trigger - Inbound Email
source_md:
The Inbound Email workflow trigger allows you to automate actions whenever a new email is received on your mailboxes. Whether the sender is an existing contact or someone entirely new, this trigger gives you granular control over how inbound emails enter your workflows – so you can capture leads, route conversations, and respond faster than ever.

[동영상](https://www.youtube.com/embed/WXVSQplwD4o?&wmode=opaque)

---

**TABLE OF CONTENTS**

- [What is the Inbound Email Workflow Trigger?](#What-is-the-Inbound-Email-Workflow-Trigger?)
- [Prerequisites: Supported Email Configurations](#Prerequisites%3A-Supported-Email-Configurations)
- [Key Points: Dedicated Domains & Inbound Email](#Key-Points%3A-Dedicated-Domains-&-Inbound-Email)
- [Email Behavior Across Different Email Setups](#Email-Behavior-Across-Different-Email-Setups)
- [How to Set Up the Inbound Email Trigger in Workflows](#How-to-Set-Up-the-Inbound-Email-Trigger-in-Workflows)
- [Trigger Filters](#Trigger-Filters)
- [Advanced Settings](#Advanced-Settings)
- [Trigger Only for New Email Conversations](#Trigger-Only-for-New-Email-Conversations)
- [Custom Value Picker Fields](#Custom-Value-Picker-Fields)
- [Use Cases of the Inbound Email Trigger](#Use-Cases-of-the-Inbound-Email-Trigger)
- [Lead Capture from Cold Inbound Emails](#Lead-Capture-from-Cold-Inbound-Emails%E2%80%8B)
- [Team Routing by Inbox](#Team-Routing-by-Inbox%E2%80%8B)
- [First-Touch Autoresponder with AI](#First-Touch-Autoresponder-with-AI%E2%80%8B)
- [Subject-Driven Automations](#Subject-Driven-Automations%E2%80%8B)
- [Ops & Compliance: Attachment-Based Workflows](#Ops-&-Compliance%3A-Attachment-Based-Workflows%E2%80%8B)
- [Frequently Asked Questions](#Frequently-Asked-Questions)
- [Related Articles](#Related-Articles)

---

# **What is the Inbound Email Workflow Trigger?**

The Inbound Email trigger fires when an inbound email is received on your mailboxes. Unlike the existing Customer Replied trigger (which activates when a contact replies to a message you sent), the Inbound Email trigger is designed to capture all inbound emails – including cold emails from brand-new senders who are not yet in your CRM.

This trigger handles three types of inbound emails:

- Cold Emails – New emails from unknown senders (not in your contacts).
- Warm Emails – New emails from known senders (existing contacts in your CRM).
- Customer Replies – Replies from known senders to an existing email thread (optional, controlled via a setting).

```
Important: Only email domains configured with LC Email or Mailgun dedicated domains can track cold inbound emails with this trigger. Two-way sync (Gmail/Outlook), shared domains and other SMTP setups do not support cold inbound email capture and will only capture emails from existing contacts. Details on email behavior are shared further down.

Inbound Email Trigger works when the contact is already created.
```

---

## **Prerequisites: Supported Email Configurations**

Before configuring this trigger, ensure your sub-account has a supported email setup. The Inbound Email trigger works best for locations configured with:

- LC Email dedicated domain
- Mailgun dedicated domain

If your sub-account does not have a supported dedicated domain configured, it will not capture all types of inbound emails. You will see a banner that will appear in the trigger UI based on your configuration

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155069328830/original/-ExHmwH1X-3SKSmBBKlkgV6xbUQp5B4uKg.png?1776361155)

---

## **Key Points: Dedicated Domains & Inbound Email**

- Any email sent to your dedicated domain will be captured, regardless of the name before the @ symbol. For example, if your domain is acme.com, emails sent to sales@acme.com, support@acme.com, or random@acme.com will all be captured.
- Each sub-account should have a unique dedicated email subdomain. If the same domain is configured across multiple sub-accounts, incoming emails may be routed unpredictably.
- If a non-dedicated domain email setup is configured (e.g., Gmail / Outlook only), the user will be redirected toward email configuration or shown clear guidance that the trigger will not reliably capture cold inbound emails.

---

## **Email Behavior Across Different Email Setups**

The table below summarizes how inbound email behaves across different email configurations. This will help you understand which setups support the Inbound Email trigger.

| Email Setup Type | Cold Inbound Email Captured | Inbound Email from Existing Contact Captured |
| --- | --- | --- |
| LC Email – Shared Domain | No | Yes, for replies to emails sent from HighLevel |
| Dedicated Domain – Mailgun or LC Email | Yes | Yes |
| Two-Way Sync – Gmail / Outlook | No | Yes |
| Other SMTP – SendGrid, Custom SMTP, etc. | No | Yes |

---

## **How to Set Up the Inbound Email Trigger in Workflows**

A clean trigger setup prevents misfires and keeps your automation predictable. Follow these steps to add and configure the Inbound Email trigger.

1. Log in to your account.
2. Navigate to **Automations** > **Workflows**.
3. **Create** a new **workflow** or **open** an **existing** one.
4. Click on the **+ Add New Trigger** button > Select **Inbound Email** from the trigger list.  
     
   ![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155069126097/original/HhBLmzMnKvIwz3-CkR6DhCACLTkx5nDTTA.gif?1776177217)

6. Enter a clear Trigger Name so it is easy to identify later (e.g., “New Lead from Sales Inbox”).
7. Click**+ Add Filters** to narrow when the workflow should run (see the Trigger Filters section below for all available options).
8. Configure the Trigger Settings checkboxes (Track replies in existing threads, Automatically create a contact). See the Trigger Settings section below.
9. Click **Save** Trigger.
10. Add your relevant workflow actions (e.g., Send Email, Create Contact, Add Tag, Assign to User), then Publish the workflow.  
      
    ![](https://jumpshare.com/share/lhguEFAImsc5PoEtmJp7+/GIF+Recording+2026-10-08+at+20.06.35.gif)

---

## **Trigger Filters**

Filters let you control exactly which inbound emails should activate the workflow. You can combine multiple filters to create precise conditions. Multiple entries can be added using comma separation where supported.

|  |  |  |  |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Filter Name | Operators | Example(s) | Notes / Behavior |
| Email Sent To / Mailbox | Equals, Is any of, Contains, Does not contain | sales@acme.com (equals)    @acme.com (contains) | Equals: passes only if the specified email is present in the To / Mailbox field. Is any of: passes if ANY address in the To header matches (supports comma-separated values). Contains / Does Not Contain: substring match on each address. |
| From | Equals, Contains, Does not contain | john@lead.com    @lead.com | Always a single value. Matches the extracted email address, not the display name. Case-insensitive. |
| CC | Equals, Is any of, Contains, Does not contain | manager@acme.com  @acme.com | Equals: passes only if the specified email is present in the CC field. Is any of: passes if ANY address in the To header matches (supports comma-separated values). Contains / Does Not Contain: substring match on each address. |
| Subject | Equals, Contains, Does not contain | Contains: refund Equals: Request for Quote | Case-insensitive match. Whitespace is trimmed before comparison. |
| Body (plain text) | Contains, Does not contain | Contains: Order ID: | Matching is run on the plain-text body by default. |
| Has Attachments | Is true / Is false | TRUE | When set to true, enables attachment-specific downstream actions. |
| Replied to Workflow | Is, Is not | Select a specific workflow | Filters based on whether the message sent from a specific workflow. Useful for isolating replies to a particular automation.  Case-insensitive match. Whitespace is trimmed before |
| Contact Tag | Has tag, Does not have tag | 16\_aug\_2022 | Filters contacts by tag. Has tag: fires only if the contact has the selected tag. Does not have tag: fires only if the contact does not have the selected tag. Useful for segmenting automations by audience. |

---

## **Advanced Settings**

The Inbound Email trigger includes an Advanced Settings section (collapsible) that gives you more control over its behavior. Click the Advanced Settings chevron to expand the section.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155069328671/original/jMm4ljmIFP01BHAsRfSXs9Dnz21im7X32g.png?1776360995)

### 

### **Trigger Only for New Email Conversations**

Type: Toggle   |   Default: Off

- When OFF (default), the trigger fires for all inbound emails, including replies within existing email threads.
- When ON, the trigger fires only when a new inbound email conversation starts (i.e., a first message, not a reply to an existing thread).

This setting is useful if you want to avoid the trigger firing repeatedly for every back-and-forth reply in an ongoing conversation. Enable this toggle if your workflow should only capture the first inbound email in a thread (e.g., new lead capture, first-touch autoresponder scenarios).

---

## **Custom Value Picker Fields**

The Inbound Email trigger makes the following custom values available for use in your workflow actions and If/Else conditions. You can use these to personalize follow-up emails, route conversations, parse email content, and more.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155069328594/original/HgE5mjv6N636oyFPLUMxRwcrFCI53ByXAA.png?1776360937)

|  |  |
| --- | --- |
| Custom Value | Description |
| {{inboundEmail.messageId}} | Unique message ID of the inbound email |
| {{inboundEmail.subject}} | Subject line of the inbound email |
| {{inboundEmail.bodyPlain}} | Plain-text body content of the email |
| {{inboundEmail.bodyFullPlain}} | Full plain-text body including the entire reply thread |
| {{inboundEmail.fromEmail}} | Sender’s email address |
| {{inboundEmail.fromName}} | Sender’s display name |
| {{inboundEmail.cc}} | CC recipients of the inbound email |

---

## **Use Cases of the Inbound Email Trigger**

Use these examples as templates to build automations that match real inbound email scenarios.

### Lead Capture from Cold Inbound Emails

- Trigger: Inbound Email
- Filters: To / Mailbox = sales@yourdomain.com
- Actions: Create contact (auto), assign to pipeline stage “New Lead,” send acknowledgement email, start lead nurturing sequence.

### Team Routing by Inbox

- Trigger: Inbound Email
- Filters: To / Mailbox contains @yourdomain.com
- Actions: Use an If/Else action to check the To / Mailbox value. Route sales@ emails to the SDR queue, support@ emails to the ticket workflow, and billing@ emails to the finance team.

### First-Touch Autoresponder with AI

- Trigger: Inbound Email
- Settings: Track replies in existing threads = Off (fire only for new threads)
- Actions: Use the AI Prompt (ChatGPT) action to generate a personalized response based on the email body, then send it as an auto-reply.

### Subject-Driven Automations

- Trigger: Inbound Email
- Filters: Subject contains “refund”
- Actions: Escalate to a manager, create a support ticket, apply a “Refund Request” tag.

### Ops & Compliance: Attachment-Based Workflows

- Trigger: Inbound Email
- Filters: Has Attachments = True
- Actions: Notify the ops team, tag the contact, move the opportunity to the next pipeline stage (e.g., “Signed Docs Received”).

---

## **Frequently Asked Questions**

**Q: How is the Inbound Email trigger different from Customer Replied?**

The Customer Replied trigger fires when a contact replies to a message you have already sent. The Inbound Email trigger fires on any inbound email – including cold emails from unknown senders. If you need to capture first-contact emails or emails from people not yet in your CRM, use the Inbound Email trigger.

**Q: Which email setups support this trigger?**

Only LC Email and Mailgun dedicated domains support full inbound email capture. Two-way sync (Gmail/Outlook) and other SMTP providers will only work for emails from existing contacts in the CRM.

**Q: Will my existing Customer Replied workflows break?**

No. The Customer Replied trigger continues to work exactly as before. The Inbound Email trigger is a separate, new trigger. Your existing configurations are not affected.

**Q: Can emails fire both the Inbound Email trigger and the Customer Replied trigger?**

It is possible for an email to match both triggers if both are configured in separate workflows. To avoid conflicting scenarios, review your trigger filters and use the “Track replies in existing threads” setting to control overlap.

**Q: What happens if the same domain is configured in multiple sub-accounts?**

If the same dedicated domain is used across multiple sub-accounts, incoming emails may be routed unpredictably. Each sub-account should have a unique dedicated email subdomain to ensure reliable routing.

**Q: Can I prevent the trigger from firing on every reply in a thread?**

Yes. Uncheck the “Track replies in existing threads” setting. When disabled, the trigger fires only for new inbound emails / new threads.

**Q: Can I filter emails based on multiple criteria?**

Yes. You can combine multiple filters (e.g., To / Mailbox + Subject + Has Attachments) to create precise conditions for when the workflow should run.

---

### **Related Articles**

- [Workflow Trigger - Customer Replied](https://help.gohighlevel.com/en/support/solutions/articles/155000002677)
- [Workflow Trigger - Email Events](https://help.gohighlevel.com/en/support/solutions/articles/155000002678)
- [Dedicated Email Sending Domains Overview & Setup](https://help.gohighlevel.com/en/support/solutions/articles/48001226115)
- [Two Way Email Sync for Outlook](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/48001229663-two-way-email-sync-for-outlook?utm_source=chatgpt.com)

title_en: Communities - Use Go Live to Host Meetings & Broadcasts
source_md:
[동영상](https://www.youtube.com/embed/GJZYXNuaXdw?&wmode=opaque)

Go Live brings real-time video, audio, and chat to your HighLevel Communities so you can run interactive workshops, live Q&As, and big announcements without leaving your space. Choose a collaborative meeting room or broadcast from your favorite encoder. Sessions are powered by Media-Core for stable, low-latency streaming on web and mobile. Use Go Live to deepen engagement, keep conversations in-platform, and share optional replays with your members.

---

**TABLE OF CONTENTS**

- [What is Go Live in Communities?](#What-is-Go-Live-in-Communities?)
- [Key Benefits of Go Live in Communities](#Key-Benefits-of-Go-Live-in-Communities)
- [Meeting Room Mode](#Meeting-Room-Mode)
- [Stream Software Mode](#Stream-Software-Mode)
- [How To Use Go Live Feature in Communities](#How-To-Use-Go-Live-Feature-in-Communities)
- [Go Live on the mobile app](#Go-Live-on-the-mobile-app)
- [Frequently Asked Questions](#%E2%80%8B%E2%80%8BFrequently-Asked-Questions)
- [Related Articles](#Related-Articles)

---

# **What is Go Live in Communities?**

Go Live is HighLevel’s built-in live session experience for Communities. It lets admins host interactive meetings or broadcast a professional stream directly into any group or channel. Members can join instantly, chat in real time, react with emojis, and if enabled, watch replays later. Because it’s native, you keep attention inside your community and simplify setup for hosts and attendees.

Go Live offers two modes:

- **Meeting Room Mode:** An interactive, many-to-many live room with host controls, chat, reactions, hand raise, screen share, and dynamic layouts (Grid/Speaker).
- **Stream Software Mode:** A broadcast experience that connects to external tools like OBS, Zoom, or StreamYard via Stream Key & URL while viewers watch and chat inside your community.

---

## **Key Benefits of Go Live in Communities**

These benefits focus on outcomes—stronger participation, simpler workflows, and content you can reuse. Use the bullets below to decide when and how to use Go Live for your programs.

- **Native experience:** Members join on web or mobile without chasing links or installing extra tools.
- **Two flexible modes:** Choose interactive meetings or high-quality broadcasts based on your format.
- **Built-in engagement:** Real-time chat, emoji reactions, and hand raise keep sessions lively.
- **Host control:** Mute/unmute, grant/revoke mic/video/screen share, remove attendees, and switch layouts.
- **Recording & replay:** Optionally capture the session and share a replay for those who missed it.
- **Device flexibility:** Preview your camera/mic, choose input devices, and switch as needed.
- **Keeps attention in-platform:** Centralizes discovery, attendance, and follow-up inside your community.

---

## **Meeting Room Mode**

Use Meeting Room Mode when you want face-to-face collaboration—coaching calls, cohort workshops, or office hours. Everyone is present in the same space, with the host managing who can speak, present, or share screens.

Highlights

- Preview camera and microphone before joining.
- Distinct Host and Attendee roles with granular permissions.
- Live text chat alongside video.
- Chat supports link sharing, file pasting, and drag-and-drop uploads.
- Chat has no message size limit.
- Screen share (window or full desktop).
- Emoji reactions and Raise hand to request the mic.
- Dynamic layouts: Grid for collaboration, Speaker for presentations.
- Multi-participant support for panels and roundtables.
- Optional recording so you can post a replay after the session.

---

## **Recording layout updates**

Go Live recordings now mirror the in-call experience more closely so replays look clean and consistent.

- No black boxes when a participant turns off their camera.
- Participant tiles stay aligned and consistent.
- Participant names display correctly and stay in sync.
- Screen sharing and multi-participant sessions use an optimized layout for clearer viewing.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155064279670/original/WV9GrTt68zyTysMVT-hjKXI1Vufy2SvOSw.png?1770302826)

---

## **Stream Software Mode**

Choose this when you already produce video through external software (OBS, Zoom, StreamYard). You’ll connect your encoder using the provided Stream Key & URL, and your community will watch and interact via chat and reactions.

- Auto-generated Stream Key and Stream URL to connect your encoder.
- Low-latency playback powered by Media-Core.
- Viewer chat and emoji reactions for real-time feedback.
- Use your existing cameras, scenes, and overlays.

### **Persistent Stream Keys (Stream Software Mode)**

When you use Stream Software Mode, your Stream Key stays the same across future sessions. This helps you go live repeatedly without reconfiguring your encoder each time.

- Reuse the same Stream Key for future Go Live sessions.
- If you want a fresh key, reset your Stream Key (for example, if you shared it accidentally).

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155064279047/original/U9oXVGhfR-SFz_soc03Fcz9JJwB9sR2Nrg.png?1770302557)

---

## **How To Use Go Live Feature in Communities**

Use this guide to start a live session in a Community Group using either the built-in Meeting Room or an external Streaming Software (Zoom/OBS/StreamYard).

### **Step 1:** Open the group and start a Go Live post

1. Go to **Memberships** from your sub-account.
2. Hover on the **Communities** tab.
3. Click on **Groups**.  
     
   ![](https://jumpshare.com/share/0eW8XfW3SbvAIpwqvsrs+/Screenshot+2025-10-14+at+7.35.48%E2%80%AFPM.png)
4. On the group you want, click **Login** to enter it.  
     
   ![](https://jumpshare.com/share/jIYcCJVctvbeaxzvaNFI+/Screen+Shot+2025-10-14+at+7.39.24+PM.png)
5. Click the **Go Live** button (red video-camera icon) near the posting tab.  
     
   ![](https://jumpshare.com/share/kIKLJXu8udHcQM6URVI6+/Screen+Shot+2025-10-14+at+7.41.19+PM.png)

### **Step 2:** Fill out post details (applies to both methods)

1. On the right panel, under Add post details:  
     
   - **Enter a Title**.
   - **Enter a Description**.
2. Under Settings, choose whether to:  
     
   - **Keep livestream as post:** leave on to save the live stream as a post after it ends.
   - **Notify members you are going live:** sends in-app + push notifications to group members.
3. Under **Choose where to post** , pick the **channel** to publish the live to.
4. When are you going live? Leave as Now (default).  
     
   ![](https://jumpshare.com/share/XnNMpfdoOZ1YpIHRlGBO+/GIF+Recording+2025-10-14+at+7.50.56+PM.gif)

### **Step 3:** Choose your video source

You have two options. Pick **one** and follow its steps.

#### **Option 1 — Meeting Room**

1. In **Select video source**, choose **Meeting Room**, then click **Go live**.
2. **Allow** your browser to use **Camera** and **Microphone**.  
     
   ![](https://jumpshare.com/share/exaEgh1dAosdIDElFJvj+/Screen+Shot+2025-10-14+at+8.13.37+PM.png)
3. Member will see the live in the channel and can join by clicking the **Join****Stream** button.  
     
   ![](https://jumpshare.com/share/JnlGAZLhjihyGd2PoI1U+/Screen+Shot+2025-10-14+at+8.03.13+PM.png)
4. Once connected, you’re live. Use these controls:  
     
   - **View** (top-right): switch **Speaker** view (large active speaker) or **Gallery** view.
   - **Audio/Video devices**: choose your **microphone**, **speakers**, and **camera**.
   - **Participants**: see **Host** and **Attendees** lists.
   - As Host you can **mute/unmute**, **grant/revoke mic**, **grant/revoke camera**, **grant/revoke screen share**, or **remove** a participant.
   - **Chat**: participants can send messages, **emojis**, and **attachments** in real time.
   - **Reactions & Raise hand**: participants can react with emojis or **raise hand**.
   - **Share**: you (or an approved participant) can **share screen**.
   - **Pin**: use the **three dots** on a tile to **Pin** a speaker to the stream.

9. When you exit a Meeting Room as the host, choose the option that matches what you want to do:

   - **End Meeting for All** ends the meeting immediately for everyone.
   - **Leave** lets the meeting continue after you assign another participant as the new host.  
       
       
     ![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155079559993/original/i2Q1c9LEMGC0EWMjNTvC5-jMYp-MMg8iiQ.png?1787926591)  
     **Leave a Meeting and Assign a New Host**  
     To leave an active meeting without ending it for everyone:  
       
     1. Select **Leave**.
     2. Search for and select a participant to become the new host.
     3. Assign the participant as host.
     4. Leave the meeting.  
          
        The selected participant receives host privileges so the meeting can continue after you exit.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155079559979/original/0b_kVEbk8FOqbrdlQdahDd2mQ7dVzhX9Mw.png?1787926572)

### **Rejoin After an Unexpected Disconnection**

If the host is disconnected unexpectedly, the meeting remains active and attendees stay connected.

This can occur after events such as a page refresh, network interruption, or device-permission issue.

The host can rejoin the same active meeting without creating a new session.

```
When the original host rejoins, host privileges automatically return to the original host. The temporary host returns to participant status.
```

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155079560628/original/vVQdsyI0kIN06qRMJMEn4qQAeRxXFvADGA.png?1787926774)

1. **After ending:**A post appears in the selected channel. It shows that the **stream ended** and the **recording is processing**; once processed, the recording is available on that post.  
     
   ![](https://jumpshare.com/share/HxK13tqLm3arBG3z8cIr+/Screen+Shot+2025-10-14+at+8.21.11+PM.png)
2. Post authors and group admins can now download recordings directly making it easier to save and share sessions.  
     
   ![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155063352378/original/CJ7NnyjbDEz4B_TLdix9Y28fOeIIW03Ajg.png?1769177647)

#### **Option 2 — Streaming Software (RTMP from Zoom/OBS/StreamYard)**

1. In **Select video source**, choose **Streaming software**.
2. Copy the provided **Server URL** and **Stream Key**.
3. In your streaming app (Zoom/OBS/StreamYard), paste the **Server URL** and **Stream Key** into its RTMP/custom streaming settings.
4. Start the **broadcast** in your streaming software.
5. Back in HighLevel, start the **Go live**; your broadcast will appear **live** in the chosen channel.  
     
   ![](https://jumpshare.com/share/SH0dgEtxSWSfyClIc98n+/Screen+Shot+2025-10-14+at+8.28.02+PM.png)

---

## **Go Live on the mobile app**

You can host or join Go Live sessions from the HighLevel mobile app. This lets you run live meetings or broadcasts without switching devices.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155063351813/original/CO6I283poJ4Nqb0wvIE0rUl9KznzCXRR6w.png?1769177360)

---

## **Frequently Asked Questions**

**Q: What’s the difference between Meeting Room and Stream Software modes?**

Meeting Room is interactive—great for workshops and coaching. Stream Software brings in a broadcast from tools like OBS or Zoom while members watch and chat.

**Q: Do members need to install anything to join?**

No extra installs are required. Members can join from supported desktop browsers or the HighLevel mobile app when signed in.

**Q: Can I record a session and share a replay?**

Yes. When recording is enabled, a replay can be shared with your members after processing, so anyone who missed the live session can catch up.

**Q: Can I restrict access to live sessions?**

Yes. Host Go Live inside private channels or paid groups so only the right members can join. Pair with Community Events for scheduling and reminders.

**Q: What if my encoder won’t connect in Stream Software Mode?**

Double-check the Stream URL/Key, confirm you selected Stream Software Mode, and start your broadcast from the encoder. Test a few minutes before showtime.

**Q: Is there chat moderation?**

Hosts can oversee chat during the session, remove disruptive participants, and manage speaking permissions to keep the event smooth.

**Q: Can I bring in guest speakers?**

Yes. Invite guests to join and assign host/speaking permissions during the session for full control.

**Q: Who can download Go Live recordings?**

Post authors and group admins can download recordings.

**Q: Why didn’t my session record?**

If a session ends due to inactivity, the app shows a message that the session wasn’t recorded due to inactivity.

**Q: Do I need a new Stream Key every time I go live?**

No. Stream Software Mode uses a persistent Stream Key, so you can reuse it for future sessions. You can reset the key if needed.

**Q: Is there a maximum number of participates or maximum amount of time you can go live?**

No. There is not a cap on the number of participants or a maximum length of a stream.

---

## **Related Articles**

- [How to Setup, Customize, and Manage Your Communities](https://help.gohighlevel.com/en/support/solutions/articles/155000000280)
- [Communities: Announcement Channel and Notification](https://help.gohighlevel.com/en/support/solutions/articles/155000005145)
- [Unified Search for Posts and Comments in Communities](https://help.gohighlevel.com/en/support/solutions/articles/155000004642)
- [How to make your Groups private/ public in Communities?](https://help.gohighlevel.com/en/support/solutions/articles/155000000735)
- [Content Management in Communities](https://help.gohighlevel.com/en/support/solutions/articles/155000000297)

title_en: Prospect AI Activity Center & CRM Pipeline Integration
source_md:
PROSPECT AI

Prospect AI Activity Center & CRM Pipeline Integration

Monitor AI agent activity, review execution history, and automatically add newly discovered prospects to a CRM pipeline and stage.

What You'll Learn

Prospect AI helps you discover business leads and monitor the performance of your AI agents. The redesigned experience introduces detailed execution history, improved agent dashboards, and recommendations for refining prospect discovery.

Native CRM pipeline integration can automatically add newly discovered prospects to a selected pipeline and stage. Learn how to review agents, investigate unsuccessful runs, view discovered prospects, and configure pipeline integration in HighLevel.

# What Is the Prospect AI Activity Center & CRM Pipeline Integration?

The Prospect AI Activity Center provides visibility into how your AI agents discover business prospects. You can review execution history, upcoming schedules, prospect counts, discovered business categories, and recommendations when an agent does not find prospects.

Selecting an agent opens its dedicated workspace with Summary and Activity tabs rather than immediately entering edit mode. The redesigned dashboard also provides agent metrics and search.

CRM pipeline integration connects prospect discovery with HighLevel's sales process. When configured within a sub-account, an agent can automatically add newly discovered prospects to a selected pipeline and stage.

## Key Benefits of Prospect AI Activity Center & CRM Pipeline Integration

The redesigned Prospect AI experience makes it easier to review agent performance, investigate unsuccessful runs, and organize prospects for follow-up.

- **Enhanced Agent Cards:** Review prospect totals, recent execution information, upcoming schedules, and agent specialization without opening the editing screen.
- **Summary and Activity Views:** Review configuration, prospect statistics, discovery criteria, and execution history before making changes.
- **Actionable Diagnostics:** Understand why an agent found no prospects and review suggested adjustments.
- **Dashboard Visibility:** See agent totals, active agents, discovered prospects, monthly lead usage, and search controls.
- **CRM Pipeline Integration:** Route newly discovered prospects to an existing sub-account pipeline and stage.

CONNECTED PROSPECTING

From Discovery to Pipeline

Prospect AI combines automated prospect discovery with CRM pipeline management so teams can organize new leads for follow-up.

## Prerequisites and Limitations

Prospect AI access and CRM routing depend on the account's Prospecting configuration. Review these requirements before enabling automatic pipeline placement.

- **Prospecting access:** Prospecting and Prospect AI must be available in the applicable account.
- **Sub-account requirement:** Native Prospect AI pipeline routing is supported for agents configured within a sub-account. Agency-level agents do not support this option.
- **Existing pipeline:** The sub-account must have a CRM pipeline and the destination stage you want to use.
- **Contact creation:** Enable **Save new prospects to Contacts** when configuring pipeline placement for the AI agent.
- **Future prospects:** Pipeline changes apply to prospects discovered after the settings are saved. Existing prospects are not automatically moved.
- **Usage limits:** Monthly lead limits and Prospect AI availability depend on the account's Prospecting access.

**Important:**

Automatic routing from Prospect AI is different from manually adding a prospect to a pipeline during a Prospecting search.

## How to Set Up Prospect AI Activity Center & CRM Pipeline Integration

Use the Prospect AI dashboard to review agent activity. To automatically route newly discovered prospects to CRM, open an existing agent and configure its Lead enrichment settings.

### Review Agent Activity and Prospect Results

The agent workspace lets you review configuration and execution results before editing an agent.

1. Open the relevant HighLevel **Sub-Account**.
2. Select **Marketing** from the left navigation.
3. Open **Prospecting**.
4. Select the **Prospect AI** tab.

![Sub-account navigation showing the Prospecting and Prospect AI location](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155076982037/original/K9pTMmJsYrtC1zczp8jTXNB0lFMLiRMpgA.png?1785211798)

5. Locate the AI agent you want to review on the dashboard.
6. Select the agent's card to open the **Agent details** panel.
7. Select **Summary** to review prospect statistics, criteria, and scheduling.
8. Select **Activity** to review historical runs and upcoming schedules.
9. Review any unsuccessful runs and the available recommendations.

**New to Prospect AI?** If no agents exist, you can use the available agent creation option. Depending on the dashboard state, it may appear as **Create your first AI Agent** or **New AI sales agent**.

![Prospect AI screen showing the option to create an AI agent](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155076982046/original/NaDyirNhsetP4KwlBZirlCjNCqgCmkR9-Q.png?1785211840)

### Configure CRM Pipeline Integration for an Existing Agent

Pipeline integration is configured separately for each eligible agent. Follow these steps to choose the pipeline and stage for future discoveries.

1. Open the relevant HighLevel **Sub-Account**.
2. Select **Marketing**.
3. Open **Prospecting**.
4. Select the **Prospect AI** tab.
5. Select an existing AI agent.
6. In the **Agent details** panel, click **Edit**.

![Agent details panel displaying the Edit action](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155076982084/original/8DchOssOWyINnJytmzjSjPkVBEiu8i4HZw.png?1785211935)

7. Open the **Lead enrichment** step in the agent editing screen.
8. Turn on **Save new prospects to Contacts**.
9. Check **Also add to a pipeline stage**.
10. Use **Pipeline name** to select the destination pipeline.
11. Use **Stage** to select the destination stage.
12. Click **Update agent** to save the changes.

![Lead enrichment settings showing Save new prospects to Contacts, Also add to a pipeline stage, Pipeline name, and Stage selectors](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155076982113/original/ucZGQziSCB3u1m1Bsg5Bk3j5vTOfEy37Qg.png?1785212125)

Configuration Applied

New prospects discovered by the configured agent can be added to the selected CRM pipeline and stage. Previously discovered prospects are not moved automatically.

## Redesigned AI Agent Cards

Redesigned agent cards display information directly on the Prospect AI dashboard. Each card helps you identify the agent and review its recent results without opening the editing screen.

**Total Prospects Discovered**

The total number of prospects discovered by the agent.

**Last Run**

The most recent execution information shown on the card.

**Next Scheduled Run**

When the agent is expected to run again.

**Agent Description and Specialization**

The agent's purpose and the types of businesses it targets.

**View Prospects**

Opens the list of prospects discovered by that agent.

![Prospect AI dashboard displaying agent cards, last run, next run, total prospects, and View prospects](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155076981556/original/x4AxuDd0Yf9JXTvdRG_rZO-TlDhZOx8Nbg.png?1785210009)

### View All Prospects Discovered by an Agent

Use the View prospects action to open a list of businesses discovered by a specific AI agent. The list shows available prospect details and provides a search field.

1. Open your HighLevel **Sub-Account**.
2. Select **Marketing**, then **Prospecting**.
3. Open the **Prospect AI** tab.
4. Locate the agent whose discoveries you want to review.
5. Click **View prospects** on the agent card.
6. Review the **List of prospects** side panel. Use **Search prospect** to find a business in the list.

![Prospect AI List of prospects panel showing discovered businesses and the prospect search field](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155084458543/original/9fd71DgvAy8CdjKxC9xMF_eaqVwZXtwVxg.png?1793248582)

## Summary and Activity Tabs

Selecting an agent opens its details panel instead of immediately entering edit mode. The Summary and Activity tabs provide different views of configuration and performance information.

### Summary Tab

The Summary tab provides a snapshot of the agent's configuration, discovered prospects, finding criteria, and upcoming schedule.

- **Prospect information:** Review the total discovered prospects and available business-category breakdowns.
- **Prospect finding criteria:** Review settings such as search radius, website requirements, Google Business Profile rating, and conversion criteria.
- **Scheduling:** Review the agent's schedule and next planned run.
- **View all prospects:** Open the list of businesses discovered by the agent.

![Agent Summary tab showing prospect statistics, discovery criteria, scheduling, and View all prospects](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155076981584/original/vusSgTlAbaBYOCqSSdTZlwI7tdtb1YP_KA.png?1785210081)

### Activity Tab

The Activity tab shows previous runs, upcoming schedules, results, and available diagnostic information. It helps you understand how an agent has performed over time.

- **Execution history:** Review previous runs and recorded results.
- **Run status:** Use the available All, Success, and Failed views to review results.
- **Upcoming schedules:** See when the next agent run is planned.
- **No-prospects-found details:** Review available explanations and recommended fixes.

![Agent Activity tab showing past runs, upcoming schedules, run statuses, and recommended fixes](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155076981596/original/Q38XSWeNqPLkcdhNdorlPWi6Dh6I11NX8w.png?1785210106)

## Agent Activity Center and Recommendations

The Agent Activity Center shows what your agents have done during previous executions. When an agent finds no prospects, the Activity tab can explain the outcome and suggest adjustments for future discovery.

- **Last execution:** Review the most recent recorded run.
- **Next scheduled run:** Review the next planned execution.
- **Prospects found:** See how many qualifying prospects were discovered.
- **Business categories:** Review the types of businesses discovered.
- **Execution logs:** Review historical results and available explanations.

### Actionable Recommendations

When an agent finds no prospects, it may recommend adjusting targeting filters or reviewing available lead limits.

**Increase Search Radius**

Expand the geographic area considered by the agent.

**Relax Conversion Score Filters**

Broaden the criteria used to qualify businesses.

**Lower Google Business Profile Rating Requirements**

Allow businesses with lower ratings to qualify.

**Review Monthly Lead Limits and Allocation**

If recommended, consider increasing the monthly lead limit or adjusting lead allocation across agents, where supported.

![Animated Agent Activity Center showing execution history and recommendations for unsuccessful runs](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155076981606/original/gd6-ssGhaeMjPuo5Sq4bG2KYSna7wlvAbg.gif?1785210184)

## Dashboard Metrics and Search

The Prospect AI dashboard provides a summary of your AI agents and their discovery results. Use the metrics, search field, and agent filter to review agents without opening each workspace.

**Total agents:** The number of configured AI agents.

**Active agents:** The number of active AI agents.

**Prospects found:** The total number of prospects discovered across agents.

**Total leads generated this month:** The number of leads generated during the current month compared with the available monthly allowance.

### Search and Filter Agents

Use **Search for an agent** to find an agent in the dashboard. The adjacent **All agents** selector provides the available agent filtering options.

![Prospect AI dashboard showing total agents, active agents, prospects found, monthly lead usage, agent search, and filters](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155076981987/original/MrUSGzLtn2swKRFEwk_JNUD8tC_MUQtGQg.png?1785211674)

## Frequently Asked Questions

Q: Do I need to create a new agent to use the Activity Center?

No. Open an existing agent to review its Summary and Activity tabs.

Q: Where can I review previous AI agent runs?

Select an agent on the Prospect AI dashboard, then open the Activity tab. Review previous executions, upcoming schedules, and available results.

Q: Why is my AI agent finding no prospects?

The Activity tab can explain why a run found no results. Review the recommendations, including possible adjustments to search radius, conversion score, and rating filters.

Q: Can Agency-level Prospect AI agents automatically route prospects to pipelines?

No. Native pipeline routing is available for eligible agents configured within a sub-account.

Q: Does changing an agent's pipeline configuration move previously discovered prospects?

No. The updated configuration applies to newly discovered prospects. Previously discovered prospects are not retroactively moved.

Q: How do I view all prospects discovered by one agent?

From Marketing > Prospecting > Prospect AI, locate the agent and select View prospects. Review or search the businesses displayed in the side panel.

Q: What button saves changes when editing an existing agent?

Select **Update agent** at the bottom of the editing screen.

title_en: Expanded Custom Field Types for Opportunities in HighLevel
source_md:
Expanded custom field types are now supported for Opportunities in HighLevel, giving teams more flexibility to capture and manage deal-specific information. Store proposal URLs, contract dates, formatted deal summaries, team assignments, and visual service selections directly on opportunity records. These fields also support Opportunity List View columns and Advanced Filters, making deal information easier to organize and access.

```
This update is available for Contacts earlier, now its available in oppurtunities.
```

---

**TABLE OF CONTENTS**

- [What Are Expanded Custom Field Types?](#What-Are-Expanded-Custom-Field-Types?)
- [Key Benefits of Expanded Custom Fields for Opportunities and Contacts](#Key-Benefits-of-Expanded-Custom-Fields-for-Opportunities-and-Contacts)
- [Supported Custom Field Types and Configuration Options](#Supported-Custom-Field-Types-and-Configuration-Options)
- [Mobile and Snapshot Support](#Mobile-and-Snapshot-Support)
- [How to Set Up Expanded Custom Fields for Opportunities](#How-to-Set-Up-Expanded-Custom-Fields-for-Opportunities)
- [How To Set Up Expanded Custom Fields](#How-To-Set-Up-Expanded-Custom-Fields)
- [Display and Filter Custom Fields in Opportunity List View](#Display-and-Filter-Custom-Fields-in-Opportunity-List-View)
- [Frequently Asked Questions](#Frequently-Asked-Questions)
- [Related Articles](#Related-Articles)

---

# **What Are Expanded Custom Field Types?**

Expanded custom fields provide additional options for collecting, validating, and displaying information in HighLevel. Previously available for Contacts, these capabilities now extend to Opportunities, allowing you to manage important deal information without relying on contact fields or unstructured notes.

The expanded field types include URL, Date & Time, Rich Text, User, and visual Checkbox and Radio Select options.

---

## **Key Benefits of Expanded Custom Fields for Opportunities and Contacts**

Expanded custom fields help teams maintain accurate information, collaborate on deals, and quickly identify important opportunity details.

- **Centralized Deal Information:** Store proposal links, contract dates, and deal summaries directly on opportunities.
- **Better Team Collaboration:** Associate multiple team members with deals using User fields.
- **Flexible Formatting:** Organize detailed deal information using Rich Text.
- **Visual Selections:** Use images and icons to identify services, priorities, and categories.
- **Improved Pipeline Visibility:** Display custom fields in List View and use Advanced Filters.
- **More structured URL collection:** Capture website addresses, profile URLs, resource links, and other URLs using a dedicated field with domain controls.
- **Greater control over dates and times:** Choose whether a field captures a date and time, date only, or time only, and control which dates can be selected.
- **Improved team collaboration:** Use Users fields to associate one or multiple team members with a record and provide selected users with follower-level access.
- **More recognizable radio choices:** Add images or icons to radio button options when users need to select a single choice.
- **Mobile Field Updates:** View and edit supported custom fields directly on contact and opportunity records in the mobile app.

---

## **Supported Custom Field Types and Configuration Options**

Each expanded field type offers different configuration options to help capture information in the most appropriate format. Selecting the right field type improves consistency and makes opportunity details easier to review.

| Field Type | Configuration Options | Opportunity Use Case |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **URL** | Allow all domains, allow only specified domains, or block specified domains | Proposal and contract links |
| **Date & Time** | Date only, time only, or both; past/future dates, date ranges, and weekdays | Contract start dates and project deadlines |
| **Rich Text** | Text formatting, headings, lists, links, and emojis | Deal summaries and scope notes |
| **User** | Single-user or multiple-user selection | Sales and implementation teams |
| **Checkbox** | Text with image; multiple selections | Services included in a deal |
| **Radio Select** | Text with image or icon; single selection | Deal priority or service package |

**Important Configuration Details**

- **URL Validation:** URLs that violate domain restrictions are rejected with the message: "This URL isn't allowed. Use an allowed domain."
- **Date Restrictions:** Future Dates Only excludes today. Select Any Date if today's date should be allowed.
- **Rich Text:** Supports bold, italics, underline, strikethrough, colors, highlighting, lists, links, emojis, and headings using `#` or `##`.
- **User Fields:** Selected users receive follower-level access without becoming the opportunity owner. The Allow multiple users setting cannot be changed after field creation.
- **Visual Options:** Checkbox fields support images, while Radio Select fields support images or icons.

For additional details about field configuration, mobile editing, and snapshot support, see [Expanded Custom Field Types and Configuration Options](https://help.gohighlevel.com/en/support/solutions/articles/155000008811-expanded-custom-field-types-and-configuration-options).

---

## **Mobile and Snapshot Support**

Expanded custom fields can also support mobile record management and reusable configurations across HighLevel locations. This helps teams maintain consistent information when working from different devices or setting up new sub-accounts.

- **Mobile:** Supported expanded fields can be viewed and edited on Contact and Opportunity records in the mobile app. Configured validation rules also apply.
- **Snapshots:** Supported expanded custom fields and configurations, including URL restrictions, date settings, and visual options, can be included in snapshots.

---

## **How to Set Up Expanded Custom Fields for Opportunities**
