  - [Quota Usage:](#Quota-Usage%3A)
  - [Using the Insights:](#Using-the-Insights%3A)
- [**Keyword Rank Tracking: Monitor Your SEO Progress**](#Keyword-Rank-Tracking%3A-Monitor-Your-SEO-Progress)
  - [Setting up Rank Tracking:](#Setting-up-Rank-Tracking%3A)
  - [Quota and Limits:](#Quota-and-Limits%3A)
- [Maximizing Value from Rank Tracking](#Maximizing-Value-from-Rank-Tracking)
- [Best Practices & Saving Lookups](#Best-Practices-&-Saving-Lookups)
- [Troubleshooting & FAQs for Keywords Tools](#Troubleshooting-&-FAQs-for-Keywords-Tools)

---

## **Keyword Research: Discover SEO Opportunities**

The Keyword Research tool allows you to search for keyword ideas along with important metrics (like search volume, difficulty, CPC, etc.). It’s similar to tools like SEMrush’s Keyword Magic or Ahrefs’ Keyword Explorer.

### **How to use Keyword Research in GHL:**

1. **Open the Advanced SEO:**  
   Go to **Keywords > Keyword Research**
2. **Enter a Seed Keyword:**  
   Type a broad term related to your niche (e.g., “teeth cleaning”). You can also enter a competitor’s domain if supported.
3. **Specify Location/Language (if available):**  
   Filter results by country or language (e.g., “United States - English”).
4. **Initiate Search:**  
   Click search to fetch related keyword suggestions.
5. **Analyze Results:**  
   Columns may include:

   - Keyword
   - Search Volume
   - Keyword Difficulty
   - CPC
   - Trend
   - Intent
6. **Refine and Filter:**  
   Narrow results using filters (e.g., volume > 100, difficulty < 50).
7. **Select Keywords of Interest:**  
   Save to a list or note them down for future use.

**Example:**  
You search “teeth cleaning” and receive 200 suggestions like “teeth cleaning cost” with 1,000 searches/month and moderate difficulty - a potential content topic to save.

---

### **Quota Usage:**

- You get **100 Keyword Research lookups per month**.
- Each search = 1 credit, but may return dozens/hundreds of suggestions.
- Be smart with usage:

  - Avoid redundant seeds (e.g., “dentist” vs. “dentistry”).
  - Use filtering to dig deeper without more queries.
  - Use a mix of broad terms, questions, and competitor domains.

---

### **Using the Insights:**

Aim to build a target keyword list for content or optimization:

- **Long-tail keywords:** Ideal for blogs and FAQ pages.
- **Buyer intent keywords:** Great for conversions.
- **Questions:** Excellent for blog/Q&A/FAQ schema.
- **High-volume core keywords:** Ensure your main pages cover these.

You can run more searches for subtopics or explore “Questions” and “Related” tabs (each may count as a separate lookup).

---

## **Keyword Rank Tracking: Monitor Your SEO Progress**

Once you have your keyword list, the Rank Tracking tool helps you monitor performance over time.

### **Setting up Rank Tracking:**

1. **Create a Rank Tracking Project:**  
   Go to **Keywords > Rank Tracker** in Advanced SEO. Click “New Project”.
2. **Name the Project** (e.g., your website or client).
3. **Specify the Domain** to track (e.g., `example.com`).
4. **Select Search Engine and Location** (e.g., Google US, or city/state for local relevance).
5. **(Optional)** Set competitors or tags.
6. **Add Keywords to Track:**  
   Paste keywords (from research or GSC). You can group by tags/topics.
7. **Set Update Frequency:**  
   Choose Daily, Every 3 Days, Weekly, or Manual. Weekly is ideal for most.
8. **View Rank Tracking Data:**  
   Columns include:

   - Current Rank
   - Change
   - Base Rank / Start
   - Best Rank
   - Search Volume
   - URL (if applicable)
   - Last Checked
9. **Charts and Trends:**  
   View trend lines per keyword and project-wide metrics (e.g., # of keywords in top 10).
10. **Competitor Tracking:**  
    If added, compare your ranks with theirs.

---

### **Quota and Limits:**

- You can **track up to 5 projects** and **1,000 keywords total**.
- Rank tracking is a continuous quota (not monthly reset).
- You can swap keywords in/out, but can’t exceed 1,000 simultaneously.

**Tips:**

- Track only the keywords that matter most.
- Weekly checks are often enough.
- GSC tracks 10k keywords passively – use that for discovery, not manual tracking.

---

## **Maximizing Value from Rank Tracking**

- **Focus on Important Keywords:** Track high-value or competitive keywords.
- **Leverage GSC Auto-Tracking:** Use manual tracking for strategic terms only.
- **Tag and Segment:** Filter by service, intent, etc.
- **Monitor Competitors:** Spot opportunities or threats by comparing trends.
- **Use Alerts (if available):** Get notified about rank drops or gains.
- **Report Progress:** Show rank improvements in client/internal reports.

---

## **Best Practices & Saving Lookups**

- **Plan Your Research Queries:** Stick to 5–10 quality seed terms for new projects.
- **Combine Research with Content Planner:** Use Content Planner’s clustering to reduce manual lookups.
- **Update Rank Tracking Wisely:** Daily isn’t necessary for all keywords.
- **Rotate Seasonal Keywords:** Swap in campaign terms when relevant.
- **Review GSC Keywords:** Use these insights to guide future research or tracking.

---

## **Troubleshooting & FAQs for Keywords Tools**

- **No Suggestions Found:** Try a broader or better-spelled keyword.
- **Volume/Difficulty Seems Off:** Use GHL data directionally; it may not match other tools.
- **Rank Tracker Not Updating:** Ensure it’s scheduled; run manual update if needed.
- **Site Not Ranking:** You may be outside top 100 results – optimize or hold off tracking.
- **Competitor’s Site Showing:** Ensure you added the correct domain.
- **Removing a Keyword:** Frees up a slot but erases history – export if needed.
- **Local vs National Tracking:** Use Local SEO (heatmaps) for Map Pack rankings; Rank Tracker is for organic results.

---

Armed with keyword research and tracking, you can identify where to compete and measure your progress in the rankings.

title_en: How to Set Up Contact and Opportunity Triggers for Managed Agents in HighLevel
source_md:
Managed Agents (formerly Super Agents) can automatically execute when contacts or opportunities are created or when opportunity statuses change in HighLevel. These CRM-based triggers help automate lead qualification, sales follow-ups, and customer onboarding without manual intervention.

---

**TABLE OF CONTENTS**

- [What Are Contact and Opportunity Triggers?](#What-Are-Contact-and-Opportunity-Triggers?)
- [Key Benefits of Contact and Opportunity Triggers](#Key-Benefits-of-Contact-and-Opportunity-Triggers)
- [Contact Created Trigger](#Contact-Created-Trigger)
- [Opportunity Created Trigger](#Opportunity-Created-Trigger)
- [Opportunity Status Changed Trigger](#Opportunity-Status-Changed-Trigger)
- [How to Set Up Contact and Opportunity Triggers](#How-to-Set-Up-Contact-and-Opportunity-Triggers)
- [Frequently Asked Questions](#Frequently-Asked-Questions)
- [Related Articles](#Related-Articles)

---

# **What Are Contact and Opportunity Triggers?**

Contact and Opportunity Triggers allow Managed Agents to execute automatically when specific CRM events occur. They extend existing triggers such as Chat, Form Submitted, Tag Changed, Appointment, and Schedule.

Three triggers are available:

- **Contact Created:** Executes an agent when a new CRM contact is created.
- **Opportunity Created:** Executes an agent when a new opportunity is created, with pipeline and stage filters.
- **Opportunity Status Changed:** Executes an agent when an opportunity changes status, with pipeline, stage, and status filters.

---

## **Key Benefits of Contact and Opportunity Triggers**

CRM-based triggers help Managed Agents respond to customer lifecycle events automatically, reducing repetitive work and improving sales processes.

- **Automated CRM Workflows:** Execute agents when contacts or opportunities are created or updated.
- **Faster Lead Engagement:** Initiate lead qualification, welcome journeys, and onboarding.
- **Targeted Automation:** Use pipeline, stage, and status filters to control agent execution.
- **Reduced Manual Tasks:** Automate follow-ups and other repetitive CRM activities.
- **Improved Sales Processes:** Support sales handoffs, win-back campaigns, and post-sale activities.

---

## **Contact Created Trigger**

The Contact Created trigger automatically executes a Managed Agent whenever a new contact is created in the CRM. It requires no additional trigger-specific configuration.

**Common use cases:**

- Welcome journeys
- Lead enrichment and qualification
- Customer onboarding

## **Opportunity Created Trigger**

The Opportunity Created trigger executes a Managed Agent when a new opportunity is created. Pipeline and stage filters help target opportunities relevant to your sales process.

**Available filters:**

- **Pipeline:** Select the relevant sales pipeline.
- **Opportunity Stage:** Select the applicable stage.

**Common use cases:**

- New opportunity qualification
- Sales notifications
- Pipeline-specific follow-ups

## **Opportunity Status Changed Trigger**

The Opportunity Status Changed trigger executes a Managed Agent when an opportunity changes status. Filters help automate actions based on specific sales outcomes.

**Available filters:**

- **Pipeline:** Select the relevant pipeline.
- **Opportunity Stage:** Select the applicable stage.
- **Opportunity Status:** Select Open, Won, Lost, or Abandoned.

**Common use cases:**

- Post-sale onboarding when an opportunity is Won
- Follow-ups for Lost opportunities
- Sales handoffs and CRM updates

---

## **How to Set Up Contact and Opportunity Triggers**

Configuring the correct trigger ensures your Managed Agent responds to the intended CRM event. Opportunity filters provide additional control over when the agent executes.

1. Navigate to **AI Agents → Agent Studio** in your HighLevel sub-account.
2. Open an existing **Managed Agent** or create a new one.
3. Open the **Trigger Picker**.
4. Select **Contact Created**, **Opportunity Created**, or **Opportunity Status Changed**.  
     
   ![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155083882748/original/VCCn1klXx4k44kylG8q3T8k5JKerDnzUuw.gif?1792593619)
5. Configure the applicable trigger:

   - **Contact Created:** No additional trigger-specific configuration required.
   - **Opportunity Created:** Configure Pipeline and Opportunity Stage filters.
   - **Opportunity Status Changed:** Configure Pipeline, Opportunity Stage, and Opportunity Status filters.
6. Configure the agent's instructions and required tools.
7. Save your changes and test the trigger using a sample contact or opportunity.
8. Publish the agent and review its executions in the **Activity** tab.

```
Note: The opportunity filter fields are supported options. Follow any required-field indicators displayed in Agent Studio.
```

---

## **Frequently Asked Questions**

**Q: Does Contact Created require additional configuration?**

No. Contact Created does not require additional trigger-specific configuration.

**Q: Can I filter which opportunities trigger my agent?**

Yes. Opportunity Created supports pipeline and stage filters. Opportunity Status Changed also supports a status filter.

**Q: Which opportunity statuses are supported?**

Open, Won, Lost, and Abandoned.

**Q: Do these triggers replace existing Managed Agent triggers?**

No. They expand existing options such as Chat, Form Submitted, Tag Changed, Appointment, and Schedule.

**Q: How can I verify that my agent executed?**

Open the Managed Agent's **Activity** tab to review execution details. If the agent did not execute, verify its published state and configured trigger filters.

---

## **Related Articles**

- [Setup and Use Managed Agents in Agent Studio](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000007931-important-update-agent-studio-is-evolving)
- [Managed Agents, Conversation AI & Ask AI: What's the Difference?](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000008362-super-agents-conversation-ai-ask-ai-what-s-the-difference-)
- [Managed Agents Appointment Triggers](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000008310-appointment-triggers-in-super-agents)
- [Scheduled Triggers for Managed Agents](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000008245-scheduled-triggers-for-super-agents-in-highlevel)
- [Managed Agent Activity Feed](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000008415-managed-agent-activity-feed-monitor-debug-ai-agents)

title_en: Linking Apple Appstore account to the Whitelabel Mobile App Customizer
source_md:
# **Mobile App Onboarding Flow:** **App Store API Key, Bundle Identifier, and Firebase Configuration**

 

**Overview**

This guide explains every action you need to take in HighLevel’s Mobile App Builder to prepare your white‑label mobile app for submission to Apple and Google..

You will:

1.**Create an App Store Connect API key** so HighLevel can automatically handle future submissions and updates.

2. **Register a unique bundle identifier** that Apple and Firebase will recognize as your app’s ID.

3. **Connect Firebase** by uploading your configuration files to enable push notifications, analytics, and crash reporting.

Completing all three steps ensures your build process is seamless and future releases require minimal effort.

### Please note

- An Apple Developer Program account with Admin access is required before you begin.
- Keep the Key ID, Issuer ID, and downloaded `.p8`  file secure; Apple only allows you to download these once.
- The bundle identifier must be unique across the entire App Store and must exactly match the IDs used in Firebase.
- Use the same Google account throughout the Firebase steps to avoid permission errors.
- If you are rebuilding an existing app, confirm that your existing app uses the same bundle identifier and Firebase project.

## **What is the AppStore Onboarding Flow?**

HighLevel’s appstore onboarding flow is a once‑per‑app wizard that collects the credentials required to compile, sign, and publish your whitelabelled mobile app on the Apple AppStore for your customers with an iOS device to download. After you finish these steps, HighLevel can build and push updates without manual intervention, and features such as push notifications will work instantly.

## 

## **How to Complete the Onboarding Flow**

### **Step 1 – Generate an App Store Connect API Key** **Video tutorial: <https://app.arcade.software/share/OYkGxoZSQrDPyo7tDDYj>**

1. **Open the Apple portal -**Go to *<https://appstoreconnect.apple.com/access/integrations/api>*. You will land on the **Users and Access › Keys**page.
2. **Choose App Store Connect API -**In the left sidebar, select **Keys** under **App Store Connect API**.
3. **Generate the key** -  Click **Generate API Key**, give the key an easily recognisable name (for example, *HighLevel Mobile App Automation*), and click **Generate**.
4. **Download the**`.p8`**file** -  The file appears once only. Save it somewhere secure such as a locked password vault.
5. **Copy the IDs** - In the key table, copy the **Key ID**. Your **Issuer ID** appears at the top of the page. You will paste both values, plus the `.p8`  file, into HighLevel's Mobile App Customizer.
6. **Upload in the Mobile App Customizer** -  Return to the Mobile App Builder, expand **App Store Connection**, and upload the three pieces of information.

**Quick note:**

You can use one API key for multiple apps. If a key is ever compromised, revoke it in App Store Connect and create a new one, then update the value in HighLevel.

### **Step 2 – Register the Bundle Identifier** **Video tutorial:**[**https://app.arcade.software/share/VUWqWe0qiHyZ3ImZWken**](https://app.arcade.software/share/VUWqWe0qiHyZ3ImZWken)

1. Launch the **App Setup stage** in the HighLevel wizard. You will see a field labelled Package Name / Bundle Identifier.

2. Click **Register** to open the dialog. HighLevel validates your Apple account and shows the team that will own the identifier.

3. Enter a **reverse‑DNS identifier**, for example **`com.youragency.appname`**. Stick to lowercase letters, numbers, and periods.

4. Review Apple’s definition, Click the small info icon to read Apple’s explanation of bundle identifiers and why they must be unique.

5. **Confirm and save** HighLevel registers the identifier in your Apple Developer account. If the ID is already taken, you will see an error and must choose a different string.

6. Enable capabilities (optional). If you require services such as Apple Sign‑In or Push Notifications, you can enable them later in your Apple Developer portal under Certificates, Identifiers & Profiles.

**Why this matters** - The bundle identifier ties together your code signing, push certificates, and App Store listing. Using the same ID across Apple and Firebase avoids mismatched signing errors during build time.

### **Step 3 – Upload Firebase Configuration Files**

**Video tutorial: <https://app.arcade.software/share/M0PMs6CwsZWTO4IXrx9r>**

1. **Open Firebase Console**- Go to `https://firebase.google.com/` and click Go to console. Sign in with your Google account.

2. Create or **select a projec**t Click **Add project** if this is your first time, or open an existing project that will own the app.

3. Add iOS and Android apps **Click Add App, choose iOS**, and enter the bundle identifier from Step 2.

4. Download the config files For iOS **download `GoogleService-Info.plist**`.  Keep the default file names.

5.**Upload in HighLevel** Return to the Setup Firebase stage, drag‑and‑drop files into the upload area, and click Continue.

6. Wait for validation. HighLevel parses the files and confirms that the bundle identifiers match those registered in Apple Developer. Once validated, push notifications and analytics are enabled.

**Advanced** - To enable APNs push notifications via Firebase Cloud Messaging, you can upload your `.p8` push key in the Project Settings › Cloud Messaging tab inside Firebase. HighLevel does not require this, but it allows you to send notifications from Firebase directly.

**Frequently Asked Questions**

Q: Do I need a separate API key for each app?

A: A single App Store Connect API key can authorize multiple apps. You may create additional keys if you prefer to isolate access.

Q: My bundle identifier is already in use. What should I do?

A: Append your company initials or region code, for example `com.youragency.appname.na`, until the ID is unique.

Q: I lost the `.p8` file. What now?

A: Revoke the key in \*\*App Store Connect › Users and Access › Keys\*\*, then create and upload a new key in HighLevel.

Q: Can I change the Firebase project later?

A: Yes, but you must regenerate and upload new `plist` and `json` files that reference the same bundle identifier. Remember to update your Apple Push keys if you move projects.

Q: How long does Apple review take after I finish these steps?

A: First‑time reviews typically take 1-3 business days, though the queue can be longer during holidays or major events.

title_en: Products: Manual and Smart Collections
source_md:
[동영상](https://www.youtube.com/embed/GV5UXLKKFF4?&wmode=opaque)

Manual and Smart Collections in HighLevel let you organize products efficiently—either by manually selecting them or automatically grouping them using rule-based logic. These options simplify catalog management, ensure consistent product organization, and keep your storefront automatically up to date.

---

**TABLE OF CONTENTS**

- [What Are Manual & Smart Collections?](#What-Are-Manual-&-Smart-Collections?)
  - [Key Benefits of Manual & Smart Collections](#Key-Benefits-of-Manual-&-Smart-Collections)
  - [Manual Collections](#Manual-Collections)
  - [Smart Collections](#Smart-Collections)
  - [Collection Rules and Operators](#Collection-Rules-and-Operators)
  - [Permanent Collection Type](#Permanent-Collection-Type)
  - [Configuring Manual and Smart Collections](#Configuring-Manual-and-Smart-Collections%E2%80%8B)
  - [Frequently Asked Questions](#Frequently-Asked-Questions)
  - [Related Articles](#Related-Articles)

---

# **What Are Manual & Smart Collections?**

Manual and Smart Collections are two methods of grouping products in HighLevel Stores.

A **Manual Collection** allows you to hand-pick products, while a **Smart Collection** uses predefined rules—such as price, title, or inventory—to automatically include products that match those conditions.

Both methods improve catalog structure, reduce manual updates, and maintain accurate product organization across your store.

---

## **Key Benefits of Manual & Smart Collections**

Using collections simplifies store management and enhances how products are presented.

- **Flexible organization:** Choose between curated or rule-based collections.
- **Automated updates:** Smart Collections refresh automatically when product data changes.
- **Product overlap:** Products can appear in multiple collections.
- **Improved SEO:** Add SEO titles and descriptions for better discoverability.
- **Faster merchandising:** Reuse collections across store pages, emails, and workflows.

---

## **Manual Collections**

Manual Collections are curated lists of products that you select manually. They are best for seasonal promotions, special themes, or custom assortments where specific control is required.

### **Key Details:**

- Products can be added or removed at any time.
- Items can be manually ordered via drag-and-drop.
- Ideal for fixed product sets or campaigns.

*![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155055738273/original/xg8U_WgFWGzZ1ikLhCnVXAawk4-Fv-Xl4w.png?1760110525)*

---

## **Smart Collections**

Smart Collections automatically include products based on saved conditions. They are designed for dynamic categories—such as products under a certain price, or items currently in stock.

### 

### **Key Details:**

- Conditions can be based on **Title**, **Variant Title**, **Price**, or **Inventory**.
- A product qualifies if any variant or price row matches the saved logic.
- Invalid or conflicting conditions (e.g., “Price > 100 AND Price < 50”) are blocked at save.
- Smart Collections update automatically in the background within a few minutes.
- Manual edits (additions/removals) are disabled to maintain accuracy.

**![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155055738657/original/AW1o80oHV9ZLlH9xUjIArutSlFgAEVtQCw.png?1760110729)**

---

## **Collection Rules and Operators**

Smart Collections depend on rule operators to determine which products are included. Creating valid rules ensures accurate results and prevents errors.

### **Supported Operators:**

- Equals
- Not Equals
- Greater Than / Less Than
- Contains / Does Not Contain

Multiple conditions can be combined using **AND** or **OR** logic for more precise control.

---

## **Permanent Collection Type**

Once created, the collection type—Manual or Smart—cannot be changed.

If you need to switch types later, create a new collection and replace the old one in your pages or workflows.

---

## **Configuring Manual and Smart Collections**

Setting up collections correctly ensures products appear where intended.

1. Go to **Payments → Products → Collections**.
2. Click **Create Collection**.
3. Enter a **Name**, optional **Image**, and **SEO details**.
4. Select a **Collection Type**:

   - **Manual:** Search and select products manually.
   - **Smart:** Define one or more rules (for example, *Price less than $50*).
5. Choose whether to apply **All** or **Any** conditions.
6. Click **Save**.
7. Smart Collections will process and update automatically in the background.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155055659065/original/CrQNShMdhdqm1ACJ7LMCr_3o7d2VM2fa4Q.png?1760042763)

---

## **Frequently Asked Questions**

**Can I switch a Manual Collection to Smart (or vice versa)?**

No. Once created, the collection type cannot be changed.

**What happens if no products match a Smart Collection rule?**

The collection will remain empty until a product satisfies the conditions.

**Can products belong to multiple collections?**

Yes. A product can appear in multiple collections based on selection or rule matching.

**Can I manually remove a product from a Smart Collection?**

No. Smart Collections automatically manage inclusion based on rule logic.

**How often do Smart Collections update?**

Updates occur in the background and complete within a few minutes.

**Where can I display collections?**

Collections can be displayed in Store Pages, Email Templates, and Workflows for filtering or automation.

---

### **Related Articles**

- [How to Select or Filter Products per Ecommerce Store?](https://help.gohighlevel.com/en/support/solutions/articles/155000004552)
- [New Product Collection Element and SEO Improvements](https://help.gohighlevel.com/en/support/solutions/articles/155000002527)
- [Bulk Actions on the Product Page](https://help.gohighlevel.com/en/support/solutions/articles/155000005209)
- [How to Sort and Filter Products in HighLevel Ecommerce Site Builder](https://help.gohighlevel.com/en/support/solutions/articles/155000003046)
- [WooCommerce: Import and Sync Products and Collections for E-commerce Stores](https://help.gohighlevel.com/en/support/solutions/articles/155000004714)
- [How to Suggest Related Products in Your Product Details Page](https://help.gohighlevel.com/en/support/solutions/articles/155000002834)

title_en: Affiliate Manager Public API: Overview, Endpoints, and Scopes
source_md:
The Affiliate Manager Public API lets developers and Marketplace app builders manage a location's affiliate program programmatically. Through REST API endpoints, developers can work with affiliates, campaigns, referred customers, commissions, payouts, payout methods, and affiliate media without relying solely on the Affiliate Manager UI.

The API suite includes 28 new endpoints and 4 existing endpoints that were tightened, for 32 endpoints in total. It is available in the v3 API catalog on the HighLevel Developer Marketplace.

---

## **Key Capabilities**

- Manage affiliates without the UI: Onboard, update, activate, and deactivate affiliates from your own app.
- Report on commissions and payouts: Pull commission and payout data into external dashboards, reconciliation, and finance workflows.
- Attribute conversions: Validate referral IDs and create leads from external landing pages and checkout flows to credit conversions to the right affiliate.
- Collect payout details in your own flow: Manage affiliate payout methods, including a lookup of the bank fields each country requires.

---

## **Who Can Use This Feature**

Developers and agencies building custom dashboards, CRM integrations, automated reporting, or partner apps using Affiliate Manager.

### **API Endpoint Groups**

All endpoints are available under /affiliate-manager and are organized into seven groups:

| Group | Endpoints | What you can do |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Affiliates | 10 | Create, read, update, and list affiliates. Activate or deactivate an affiliate. Move an affiliate between campaigns. Set and validate referral IDs. Suspend an affiliate from a campaign. Upload a tax form. |
| Payout Methods | 6 | Create, read, update, and delete an affiliate's payout methods. Mark a payout method as primary. Look up the bank fields required for each country. |
| Commissions | 5 | Create, list, and delete commissions. Update commission status. Deny commissions. |
| Customers | 5 | List the customers an affiliate referred. Create and validate leads. Update a customer's state. Delete a customer. |
| Affiliate Media | 3 | List, update, and delete affiliate media files and folders for a location. |
| Campaigns | 2 | List campaigns and retrieve a campaign with its commission structure. |
| Payouts | 1 | List payouts for a location. |

---

## **Important API Behaviors**

Before using the Affiliate Manager API, review these endpoint-specific behaviors:

- Creating affiliates: If an affiliate with the same email address already exists in a location, the Create Affiliate endpoint updates the existing affiliate instead of creating a duplicate.
- Updating affiliates: The Update Affiliate endpoint replaces the affiliate record. Fields omitted from the request body are cleared, so include all fields you want to retain.
- Referral IDs: Referral IDs must be unique within a location, even when affiliates belong to different campaigns.
- Suspending affiliates: Suspending an affiliate from a campaign cancels their pending and denied payouts, commissions, and transactions. Reinstating the affiliate returns canceled items to pending status.
- Payout methods: An affiliate can have one PayPal payout method and one bank payout method. The first method added becomes the primary method.
- Deleting payout methods: You cannot delete the primary payout method while the affiliate has more than one payout method.
- Payout information: The List Payout Methods endpoint returns only the last four characters of bank account values.

Refer to the [Affiliates](https://marketplace.gohighlevel.com/docs/ghl/affiliate-manager/affiliates) and [Payout Methods](https://marketplace.gohighlevel.com/docs/ghl/affiliate-manager/payout-methods) API documentation for endpoint-specific requirements.

---

## **Authentication and Scopes**

The APIs use standard v3 OAuth 2.0 with Location-Access. Two scopes control what your app can do:

- affiliate-manager.readonly: Required for the 12 endpoints that read data.
- affiliate-manager.write: Required for the 20 endpoints that create, update, or delete data.

---

## **How to Get Started**

1. Open the [Affiliate Manager API v3](https://marketplace.gohighlevel.com/docs/ghl/affiliate-manager/affiliate-manager-api-v-3) documentation in the HighLevel Developer Marketplace.
2. Create or open your app in the Developer Marketplace and enable the affiliate-manager.readonly and/or affiliate-manager.write scopes, depending on what your app needs to do.
3. Authorize your app for a location using OAuth 2.0 with Location-Access.  
   For instructions on registering an app, configuring OAuth settings, installing the app for a location, and obtaining access tokens, see the [HighLevel OAuth 2.0 documentation](https://marketplace.gohighlevel.com/docs/Authorization/OAuth2.0).
4. Call the endpoints for the group you need. Each group has its own reference page with request and response details:  
     
   - [Affiliates](https://marketplace.gohighlevel.com/docs/ghl/affiliate-manager/affiliates)
   - [Payout Methods](https://marketplace.gohighlevel.com/docs/ghl/affiliate-manager/payout-methods)
   - [Commissions](https://marketplace.gohighlevel.com/docs/ghl/affiliate-manager/commissions)
   - [Customers](https://marketplace.gohighlevel.com/docs/ghl/affiliate-manager/customers)

title_en: How InitiateCheckout and AddPaymentInfo Work in Meta Pixel Tracking
source_md:
Meta Pixel tracks checkout activity in HighLevel funnels, websites, and stores. InitiateCheckout identifies when buyers begin checkout, while AddPaymentInfo tracks when they proceed to payment. These events help you understand checkout abandonment and provide Meta with information for campaign optimization.

---

**TABLE OF CONTENTS**

- [How InitiateCheckout Tracking Works](#How-InitiateCheckout-Tracking-Works)
- [How Duplicate Events Are Prevented](#How-Duplicate-Events-Are-Prevented)
- [Abandoned-Cart Recovery](#Abandoned-Cart-Recovery)
- [Express Wallet Payments](#Express-Wallet-Payments)
- [What Information Does AddPaymentInfo Send?](#What-Information-Does-AddPaymentInfo-Send?)
- [AddPaymentInfo for Free Orders and Gift Cards](#AddPaymentInfo-for-Free-Orders-and-Gift-Cards)
- [How These Changes Affect Checkout Reporting](#How-These-Changes-Affect-Checkout-Reporting)
- [Do You Need to Update Your Meta Pixel Settings?](#Do-You-Need-to-Update-Your-Meta-Pixel-Settings?)
- [When Do Page-Level Changes Take Effect?](#When-Do-Page-Level-Changes-Take-Effect?)
- [Cookie Consent and Conversions API](#Cookie-Consent-and-Conversions-API)
- [Frequently Asked Questions](#Frequently-Asked-Questions)

---

## **How InitiateCheckout Tracking Works**

InitiateCheckout fires when a buyer starts the checkout process. The timing depends on where the event is configured and which checkout experience the buyer uses.

| Checkout Experience | When InitiateCheckout Fires |
| --- | --- |
| Store checkout page | When the checkout page loads |
| Page-level event configuration | When the configured page loads |
| Funnel-level tracking | When the buyer first interacts with an order form |
| Website-level tracking | When the buyer first interacts with an order form |
| Webinar-level tracking | When the buyer first interacts with an order form |
| One-step, two-step, popup, and new order forms | On the buyer's first click, tap, or keystroke, unless page-level tracking applies |

When InitiateCheckout is configured at the page level, the event fires on page load without waiting for an order-form interaction.

**How Duplicate Events Are Prevented**

InitiateCheckout fires at most once per page visit. This applies even when a page contains multiple order forms or more than one configured trigger. The following actions do not trigger InitiateCheckout:

- Browser autofill
- Password-manager autofill
- Automatic field focus when the page loads

**Abandoned-Cart Recovery**

When buyers return through an abandoned-cart recovery link, InitiateCheckout waits until the saved cart loads. This allows the event to include the restored cart value and products.

**Express Wallet Payments**

InitiateCheckout also tracks buyers who use express payment methods, such as Apple Pay, without interacting with the order form. In these cases, the event fires when payment begins.

---

## **What Information Does AddPaymentInfo Send?**

AddPaymentInfo sends additional order and customer information to Meta when available.

| Data | Information Sent |
| --- | --- |
| Order value | Value associated with the order |
| Currency | Order currency |
| Product IDs | Product identifiers associated with the order |
| Email | Hashed customer email |
| Phone | Hashed customer phone number |
| Name | Hashed customer name |
| External ID | Hashed customer external ID |

This additional information helps Meta match conversion events to customers and improve event attribution. Invalid or blank values are not sent. Events associated with the same order use a consistent currency.

**AddPaymentInfo for Free Orders and Gift Cards**

AddPaymentInfo is not sent when an order requires no payment details. However, orders fully covered by a gift card now send AddPaymentInfo with an order value of `0`.

---

## **How These Changes Affect Checkout Reporting**

InitiateCheckout may report more events because it now captures buyers earlier in the checkout process. Previously, InitiateCheckout and AddPaymentInfo often counted the same buyers. You can now distinguish buyers who begin checkout from those who proceed to payment.

When reviewing campaign performance, consider these changes before comparing:

- InitiateCheckout counts before and after the update
- Checkout abandonment rates
- Cost per InitiateCheckout
- Automated rules based on InitiateCheckout

An increase in InitiateCheckout events does not necessarily indicate an increase in completed purchases.

---

## **Do You Need to Update Your Meta Pixel Settings?**

No configuration changes are required. The updated tracking behavior applies automatically to supported funnels, websites, and stores with InitiateCheckout enabled. If InitiateCheckout is not enabled, this change does not affect the pixel's existing behavior.

**When Do Page-Level Changes Take Effect?**

Changes to page-level InitiateCheckout settings may take up to 24 hours to take effect on previously published pages. To apply the changes immediately, edit and save the page.

---

## **Cookie Consent and Conversions API**

The update does not change existing cookie-consent behavior. When visitors have not accepted advertising cookies, tracking events are not sent to Meta.

If Conversions API is enabled, browser and server events continue to be sent and deduplicated in Meta Events Manager. The timing of PageView, ViewContent, and Purchase events remains unchanged.

---

## **Frequently Asked Questions**

**Why did my InitiateCheckout count increase?**

InitiateCheckout now tracks buyers at the beginning of checkout rather than waiting until they proceed to payment. More buyers are included, even when they abandon checkout.

**Can InitiateCheckout fire multiple times on the same page?**

InitiateCheckout fires at most once per page visit, even when multiple order forms or triggers exist.

**Does browser autofill trigger InitiateCheckout?**

No. Browser autofill, password managers, and automatically focused fields do not trigger the event.

**Does InitiateCheckout work with Apple Pay?**

Yes. When buyers use an express payment option without interacting with the order form, InitiateCheckout fires when payment starts.

**Does the update change Purchase tracking?**

No. Purchase continues to fire at the same point as before.

**Do I need to reconnect my Meta Pixel?**

No. The update applies automatically to eligible existing configurations.

title_en: Reputation Management: New Widget Types + Full AI Summary Control
source_md:
This article introduces new updates to review widgets, including the Floating Badge Widget, Slider Widget, advanced style customization, and fully configurable AI summaries — giving you more flexibility and control to showcase customer feedback in the most impactful way possible.

# What’s New in Review Widgets?

Review widgets have received a major upgrade, making it easier than ever to display testimonials that build trust and drive conversions. With new widget types, flexible AI summary options, and a full visual style editor, you can now create beautifully branded, engaging displays without writing a single line of code.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155049540794/original/KM3YF5JCVTaxjgLgvO-K5PFnfQY-tD8-7Q.png?1751990350)

# Key Benefits of the New Review Widgets

These enhancements empower you to highlight customer feedback in more dynamic, on-brand ways — no design or technical skills needed.

- Highlight reviews anywhere on your site with flexible display options.
- Visually match your brand using deep style customization tools.
- Drive more conversions through sleek, engaging testimonial presentations.
- Save time with real-time previews and easy plug-and-play templates.
- Improve site performance thanks to optimized loading and smoother widget creation.

# Floating Badge Widget

The Floating Badge Widget is a minimal, always-visible badge that continuously rotates through your best reviews. This is perfect for discreet yet powerful social proof on any corner of your website.

# Slider Widget

The Slider Widget allows you to display one review at a time in a smooth carousel format. It’s ideal for narrower spaces or pages where you want to focus on individual stories.

- Highlight one testimonial at a time for greater impact.
- Control the slide interval to match your page’s viewing flow.
- Great for hero sections, sidebars, or focused testimonial sections.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155049540797/original/ywjgviEUZEjnVn7tzeoBvVO5ew8aJWi7WA.png?1751990350)

# 

# AI Review Summaries Now Fully Configurable

  - Short (1–2 sentences)

  - Action Points (bullet format)

  - Top of the review
  - Integrated within the review layout

```

AI Summary aligns within your selected widget layout by default. You can still choose Top placement if you prefer the summary above the reviews.
```

# 

# Using the Template Library and Style Customization

Choose from a growing library of beautifully designed templates or create your own custom design using the new visual style editor.

- Quickly swap between plug-and-play templates without coding.
- Customize colors for buttons, avatars, backgrounds, and summary text to perfectly match your brand.
- See changes instantly with the built-in real-time preview.
- No CSS or developer help needed.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155049540799/original/FMpz66XP0WRmtyUGURmLNleayWm2yyaFLg.png?1751990350)

title_en: Getting Started with Workflows
source_md:
Workflows help you automate repetitive tasks so you can save time and scale your business. Once configured, workflows run automatically based on triggers and perform a sequence of actions without manual intervention.

You can use workflows to manage leads, automate follow-ups, send communications, and streamline operations across your business.

---

**TABLE OF CONTENTS**

- [What are Workflows?](#%E2%80%8B%E2%80%8BWhat-are-Workflows?)
- [Workflow Triggers](#Workflow-Triggers)
- [Workflow Actions](#Workflow-Actions)
- [Tasks Worth Automating](#Tasks-Worth-Automating)
- [Workflow Recipes: Pre-Built Templates](#Workflow-Recipes%3A-Pre-Built-Templates)
- [How to Create a Workflow](#How-to-Create-a-Workflow)
- [Workflows Landing Page (Updated Experience)](#Workflows-Landing-Page-(Updated-Experience))
- [Types of Advanced Workflows](#Types-of-Advanced-Workflows)
- [Chaining Multiple Workflows](#Chaining-Multiple-Workflows)
- [Webhooks (Trigger & Action)](#Webhooks-(Trigger-&-Action))
- [Troubleshooting](#Troubleshooting)
- [Frequently Asked Questions](#Frequently-Asked-Questions)
- [Related Articles](#Related-Articles)

---

## **What are Workflows?**

A workflow is an automated sequence of actions triggered by a specific event.

### **Example:**

- A lead submits a form → send confirmation email + SMS
- A customer books an appointment → notify team + follow-up

Workflows consist of:

- **Trigger** → Starts the workflow
- **Actions** → Tasks performed after the trigger

---

## **Workflow Triggers**

Triggers define when a workflow begins.

### **Example:**

- Form submitted
- Appointment booked
- Payment received

### 

---

## **Workflow Actions**

Actions are the steps that occur after a trigger fires.

### **Example:**

- Send email or SMS
- Create or update contact
- Assign tasks or opportunities

### 

---

## **Tasks Worth Automating**

Automate repetitive tasks such as:

- Lead nurturing campaigns
- Appointment scheduling
- Follow-ups and reminders
- Customer onboarding
- Feedback collection
- CRM updates

Automation improves efficiency, consistency, and scalability.

---

## **Workflow Recipes: Pre-Built Templates**

HighLevel provides pre-built templates to help you get started quickly.

You can:

- Use ready-made workflows
- Customize them for your needs
- Save time building from scratch

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155070070542/original/HkTsouQ3sw38gVqbwvfduBEVZ8ScX1yTlQ.png?1777328028)

---

## **How to Create a Workflow**

Workflows are created in three main steps:

### **Step 1:**Choose a Trigger

Select the event that starts the workflow.

- Click **Add New Trigger**
- Choose from available triggers

### 

### **Step 2:**Add Trigger Filters (Optional)

Filters refine when the workflow should trigger.

### **Example:**

- Only trigger for incoming calls
- Only trigger for a specific phone number

### 

### **Step 3:**Add Workflow Actions

Actions define what happens after the trigger.

- Click **Add Action**
- Select the action you want

### 

---

## **Workflows Landing Page (Updated Experience)**

The Workflows landing page has been redesigned to make it easier to get started.

You now have three clear options:

- **Build using AI** – Describe your workflow and let AI generate it
- **Browse Templates** – Choose from pre-built workflows
- **Create Workflow** – Start from scratch

This helps new users quickly choose the best way to begin building workflows.

If AI Builder is disabled in Labs, the previous landing experience will be shown instead.

### 

---

## **Types of Advanced Workflows**

### **IF/Else Conditions**

Split contacts into different paths based on conditions.

---

## **Chaining Multiple Workflows**

You can connect multiple workflows together to automate full pipelines and customer journeys.

---

## **Webhooks (Trigger & Action)**

Webhooks allow HighLevel to communicate with external systems and automate workflows across platforms.

---

## **Troubleshooting Workflow Issues**

1. **Test with a fresh contact:** Use a new contact that has not previously entered the workflow to rule out prior enrollment or re-entry restrictions.
2. **Review trigger filters:** Confirm the contact meets all trigger conditions and filters required to enter the workflow.
3. **Check re-entry settings:** Verify whether the workflow allows the same contact to enter more than once when repeat enrollment is expected.
4. **Compare live behavior with test mode:** If the workflow works in test mode but not with a live contact, review the live trigger event and enrollment conditions.
5. **Review execution and error logs:** Check the workflow execution history for skipped steps, failed actions, or error messages that can help identify the cause.
6. **Escalate with evidence:** If the issue continues, provide the affected contact, workflow name, approximate test time, screenshots, and relevant execution or error details when contacting support.

---

## **Frequently Asked Questions**

**Q: What is the difference between a trigger and an action?**

A trigger starts the workflow when a specific event occurs, while actions are the steps that run after the trigger is activated.

**Q: Can I use multiple triggers in one workflow?**

Yes. You can add multiple triggers to a workflow, allowing contacts to enter from different sources.

**Q: Are workflow filters required?**

No, filters are optional. However, they are recommended to ensure workflows only run under specific conditions.

**Q: Can I edit a workflow after creating it?**

Yes. You can update triggers, filters, and actions at any time.

**Q: Will workflows run automatically once created?**

Yes, as long as the workflow is published and the trigger conditions are met.

**Q: What happens if a workflow is not working correctly?**

Check your trigger conditions, filters, and workflow settings. Testing with a fresh contact is also recommended.

**Q: Can I use AI to create workflows?**

Yes. The updated Workflows landing page allows you to describe your workflow and generate it using AI.

---

## **Related Articles**

- [Workflow AI Builder](https://help.gohighlevel.com/en/support/solutions/articles/155000006100)
- [Workflow Settings - Overview](https://help.gohighlevel.com/en/support/solutions/articles/48001239875)

title_en: Effortless File Search: Media Center’s File Type Filter for Quick Access
source_md:
[동영상](https://www.youtube.com/embed/6GbMrplRdpw?&wmode=opaque)

The new File Type Filter for Media Center lets you zero-in on photos, videos, audio, docs, PDFs, and more with a single click—so you spend less time scrolling and more time creating.

---

**TABLE OF CONTENTS**

- [What is the File Type Filter in Media Center?](#What-is-the-File-Type-Filter-in-Media-Center?)
- [Key Benefits of the File Type Filter](#Key-Benefits-of-the-File-Type-Filter)
- [File Type Categories](#File-Type-Categories)
- [Smart Context Awareness](#Smart-Context-Awareness)
- [Persistent Search Integration](#Persistent-Search-Integration)
- [Cross-Module Consistency](#Cross-Module-Consistency)
- [How To Set Up & Use the File Type Filter](#How-To-Set-Up-&-Use-the-File-Type-Filter)
- [Frequently Asked Questions](#Frequently-Asked-Questions)
- [Related Articles](#Related-Articles)

---

# **What is the File Type Filter in Media Center?**

File Type Filter is a dropdown control added to the Media Center toolbar that hides non-matching files and shows only the categories you choose (Photos, Videos, Audio, Docs, PDFs, Other, or All). The filter works across My Media, Google Drive, and any connected libraries, intelligently de-activating in sources where file-type filtering isn’t relevant (e.g., Unsplash).

---

## **Key Benefits of the File Type Filter**

- **Simplified file discovery:** locate the right asset in seconds
- **Cleaner workspace:**unclutter large libraries by hiding irrelevant formats
- **Fewer clicks:** apply once and keep browsing; search terms persist as you move between tabs(help.gohighlevel.com)
- **Consistent experience:** same dropdown in My Media, Google Drive, and External sources
- **Context-aware:**automatically disables when browsing image-only libraries (Unsplash, Pixabay)
- **Backend-optimised:** server-side filtering delivers results faster even in very large folders

---

## **File Type Categories**

File Type Filter groups extensions into easy-to-understand buckets so you don’t have to remember every format.

- **Photos** – JPG, PNG, SVG, GIF
- **Videos** – MP4, MOV, WEBM, AVI
- **Audio** – MP3, WAV, OGG
- **Docs** – DOCX, TXT, CSV, XLSX, PPTX
- **PDFs** – Portable Document Format files
- **Other** – ZIP, RAW, and miscellaneous formats

---

## **Smart Context Awareness**

Smart Context Awareness automatically disables the dropdown when a source already contains one file type (for example, Unsplash returns only images). This prevents confusing “empty” states and keeps the UI clean.

---

## **Persistent Search Integration**

Search terms you enter in the Media Center now “stick” as you hop between My Media, Google Drive, and External Libraries. The File Type Filter respects and preserves those search terms so you can refine results without starting over.

---

## **Cross-Module Consistency**

Because Media Center powers uploads for Social Planner, Funnels, Email Builder, Communities, and more, the File Type Filter instantly improves every workflow that opens the Media dialog. Edits you make in one module are reflected everywhere thanks to shared Media Storage infrastructure.(help.gohighlevel.com)

---

## **How To Set Up & Use the File Type Filter**

These steps focus only on using the **File Type** control so you can quickly narrow results, combine with search, and understand reset behavior across sources.

1. In **Media Storage**, locate the **File Type** dropdown in the top toolbar (beside **Sort**).
2. Click **File Type** and choose a category: **Photos**, **Videos**, **Audio**, **Docs**, **PDFs**, **Other**, or **All** (default).  
   **![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155062714550/original/goMsKWhXmElG6c5RW5VZeswsy8vrxqvM7w.png?1768471662)**
3. Browse or use **Search**; only matching files remain visible.
4. Reset options:

   - Change **File Type** back to **All** to see everything in the current source, or
   - Switch sources (**My Media**, **Google Drive**, **External Libraries**) to clear the **File Type** selection. **Search** persists.  
     ![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155062730578/original/EhW6vtnY48konJF0u5tIsO-KDBOAHwR7Mw.png?1768479554)

**Callouts**

- **Does not affect storage**: Filters change what you see, not what you store.
- **Availability**: Desktop app and web. Mobile filtering not yet available.

## 

---

## **Frequently Asked Questions**

**Q:****Does the filter affect upload limits or storage usage?**

No. It only changes what you see; storage policies remain the same.

**Q: Can I multi-select files across different types after filtering?**

Yes—switch back to All, then multi-select. Multi-select only works within the current view.

**Q: Why is the dropdown greyed out in Unsplash?**

Smart Context Awareness disables the control in sources where every file is already an image to avoid redundant filtering.

**Q: Will my filter choice sync to other team members?**

No. **File Type** is a user‑level preference and resets per session for each user.

**Q: Is the filter available in the Mobile App?**

Not yet. Mobile Media Library already includes basic search and upcoming updates will introduce mobile filtering.

**Q: Which API endpoint powers backend filtering for developers?**

MediaService → /medias?type={photo|video|audio|doc|pdf|other}. For channels authenticated with OAuth, this endpoint honors the `type` parameter consistently and can return folders (in addition to files) when a valid type is provided.

**Q: Does “Docs” include Google Docs links?**

No. Docs refers to uploaded document files (DOCX, TXT, etc.). Linked Google Docs appear under “Other.”

---

### **Related Articles**

- [Media Library – Mobile App](https://help.gohighlevel.com/en/support/solutions/articles/155000006309)
- [Media Library – Built-In Image Editor](https://help.gohighlevel.com/en/support/solutions/articles/155000006538)
- [Complete Guide to Media Storage](https://help.gohighlevel.com/en/support/solutions/articles/155000002707)
- [Media Storage & File Upload Limits](https://help.gohighlevel.com/en/support/solutions/articles/48001216629)
- [Simplify Your Template Library by Hiding Types and Tags](https://help.gohighlevel.com/en/support/solutions/articles/155000006576)

title_en: Rentals - Taxes
source_md:
[동영상](https://www.youtube.com/embed/ZSCIcTwIOY0?&wmode=opaque)

Manage rental bookings in HighLevel with transparent manual taxes in **Rentals**. This guide article what the feature is, who it’s for, how it works, and how totals appear across the booking page, booking details, invoices, and reports.

---

**TABLE OF CONTENTS**

- [What are Taxes for Rentals?](#What-are-Taxes-for-Rentals?)
  - [Key Benefits of Rental Taxes](#Key-Benefits-of-Rental-Taxes)
  - [Manual Taxes in Rentals](#Manual-Taxes-in-Rentals)
  - [Visibility in Bookings & Invoices](#Visibility-in-Bookings-&-Invoices)
  - [How To Apply Taxes to Rental Listings](#How-To-Apply-Taxes-to-Rental-Listings)
  - [Frequently Asked Questions](#Frequently-Asked-Questions)

---

# **What are Taxes for Rentals?**

Taxes in Rentals allow you to present a clean, itemized checkout experience while keeping reporting accurate. Each listing automatically creates a linked product. You can attach manual tax rate(s) to that product.

Tax rates are configured in Payments and then applied directly to Rental Listings. When a rental booking is created, the selected tax rate(s) automatically calculate and appear in:

- The public booking page
- The booking detail view
- Rental invoices
- Receipts and exports

If multiple listings are included in one booking, taxes are calculated per listing and combined into the final total.

---

## **Key Benefits of Rental Taxes**

These benefits focus on transparency, compliance, and reporting accuracy across rental transactions.

- **Manual Tax Control:**Configure manual taxes for rental listings using the linked product in Payments.
- **Transparent Pricing:** Help customers see more accurate booking totals when taxes apply to a rental booking.
- **Variant-Level Flexibility:**Apply different tax configurations when each variant has its own linked product.
- **Operational Efficiency:** Eliminate manual tax calculations and reduce workarounds during booking management.
- **Better Financial Visibility:** Ensure taxes appear in booking-related totals, invoices, and related reporting views where supported.

---

## **Manual Taxes in Rentals (v2)**

Manual taxes are attached to a Product, not directly to the listing. Because each listing has a linked product, assigning tax rate(s) to that Product ensures the correct taxes are added to the booking total every time the listing is booked.

**How it works**

- Each listing auto-creates a linked product.
- Add one or more tax rate(s) to that Product in **Payments** → **Settings** → **Taxes**.
- When the listing is booked, those tax rate(s) are applied automatically.

If tax settings are inclusive in Payments, the system extracts the tax portion from the listing price. If exclusive, the tax is added on top of the rental subtotal.

---

## **Visibility in Bookings & Invoices**

Knowing where taxes appear helps verify totals and respond to customer questions.

You’ll see taxes:

- On the public booking page (itemized above the total)
- Inside the booking edit view in Rentals
- Inside the payments tab of the booking
- On generated Invoices

The same totals carry across the Rentals module for internal reporting and reconciliation.

---

## **How To Apply Taxes to Rental Listings**

Proper setup ensures every booking reflects accurate totals, reduces customer confusion, and speeds up reconciliation. Follow these steps to configure both taxes and fees.

1. Go to **Calendars** → **Calendar Settings** → **Rentals** → **Listings** and open the listing you want to update. The Rentals listing editor includes the advanced configuration areas used to manage inventory, pricing, and related options.  
     
   ![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155071358723/original/gjmuC5uqyhKcrhISsZ3WrS8LWWQ13tf_dQ.png?1778779241)
2. Click Edit Listing  
    ![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155071358828/original/yQtN7QYjYwM1LW0ajXOK8EiLP3JHM5skyA.png?1778779295)
3. Navigate to the Inventory & Pricing tab then click **Configure Taxes for This Listing**.  
     
   ![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155071358853/original/WYltwyQV47wSoQt8juX6-E46dgZnNvCsBQ.png?1778779320)
4. HighLevel redirects you to the linked product under **Payments** > **Products**. Add or update the manual tax for the linked product. Click **Save**.  
     
   ![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155071358886/original/XBdJ6bcqyaK-0mDnhipyMR_jhlaljHKQ0A.png?1778779360)
5. Create a new booking or review a future booking total to confirm that tax is being applied as expected. Taxes apply to future bookings after configuration is saved.  
     
   ![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155071358966/original/usMg_XrQU50xow8lCAxwbgNgZ1vdW3PLnQ.gif?1778779464)

---

## **Frequently Asked Questions**

**Q: Can I use different tax rates for different listings?**

Yes. Taxes are configured per Rental Listing, so each listing can have its own tax rate(s).

**Q: Do tax changes affect past bookings?**

No. Changes apply to new bookings going forward. Existing bookings remain unchanged unless modified.

**Q: How are taxes handled in multi-listing bookings?**

Each listing calculates its tax independently. The system then combines all tax amounts into the final booking total.

**Q: Are the taxes applied on the associated security deposit too?**

No. The taxes are exclusively applied to the listing only.

**Q: Does Rentals support automatic taxes?**No. Rentals currently supports manual taxes only. 

**Q: Do taxes apply to the security deposit?**No. Taxes are applied to the listing only, not to the associated security deposit. 

---

title_en: Social Planner - Meta Threads Integration
source_md:
Threads Integration in HighLevel’s Social Planner lets you schedule, publish, and automate content on Meta’s new Threads platform without leaving your dashboard. Use this guide to connect your account, understand media limits, and leverage automation tools like Category Queues, RSS Auto-Posting, and Advanced CSV Upload to keep your Threads audience engaged.

---

**TABLE OF CONTENTS**

- [What is Threads Integration in Social Planner?](#What-is-Threads-Integration-in-Social-Planner?)
- [Key Benefits of Threads Integration](#Key-Benefits-of-Threads-Integration)
- [Threads Publishing Specifications](#Threads-Publishing-Specifications)
- [How to Connect Threads with Social Planner](#How-to-Connect-Threads-with-Social-Planner)
- [Frequently Asked Questions](#Frequently-Asked-Questions)
- [Related Articles](#Related-Articles)

---

# **What is Threads Integration in Social Planner?**

Threads Integration adds Meta’s text-centric social network to the list of channels you can manage inside HighLevel. By logging in with your Instagram credentials, you can compose, schedule, and track Threads posts alongside Facebook, Instagram, LinkedIn, and others, all from one calendar. This closes a major competitive gap and keeps your team working in a single workflow. 

---

## **Key Benefits of Threads Integration**

- **One-stop publishing:** Manage Threads alongside Facebook, Instagram, LinkedIn, and more from a single Social Planner calendar, no app switching.
- **Automation that saves hours:** Use Review Flow, RSS Auto-Posting, and Category Queues to auto-fill your calendar and keep Threads active without manual posting.
- **Scale content in minutes:** Bulk-create and schedule hundreds of posts via Advanced CSV Upload, map hashtags, categories, first comment, and more.
- **Fewer publishing surprises:** Compose within API-aligned limits (500 characters, up to 20 images or one 5-minute video) to prevent failed posts and rework.
- **Consistent brand presence:** Schedule ahead and recycle evergreen content so your Threads channel stays on-cadence, even when your team is busy.

---

## **Threads Publishing Specifications**

| **Category** | **Images** | **Video** |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **File Types** | JPEG, PNG | MP4, MOV |
| **Max File Size** | 8 MB | 1 GB |
| **Max Uploads per Post** | Up to 20 images | 20 videos (can mix with images) |
| **Dimensions / Resolution** | Min 320px, Max 1440px | Valid width upto 1920 px |
| **Aspect Ratio** | 0.01:1 to 10:1 | 0.01:1 to 10:1. |
| **Duration** | **–** | Up to 5 minutes |
| **Frame Rate** | **–** | 23–60 FPS |
| **Codecs** | **–** | H.264 or HEVC (video), AAC (audio) |
| **Other Notes** | **-** | No custom thumbnails supported |

---

## **How to Connect Threads with Social Planner**

```
Note: Your Threads account should be linked to your Instagram account, as Threads access is managed through your Instagram credentials.
```

Follow these exact steps to connect Threads:

# 1. Click on **Marketing** from your sub-account. 2. Click on the **Social****Planner** tab. 3. Click on the **+ Socials** button. 4. Click on the **Connect****Threads** option. 5. Log in with your **Instagram****credentials** and **authorize****access**. 6. Click on the **Add** button beside the profile you want to connect. 7. Once connected, your Threads account will appear under **All Accounts** drop-down in Social Planner. ``` Note: Now you can manage Threads Comments in Social Planner For supported capabilities, limitations, and detailed instructions, see Manage Comments in Social Planner ```

---

## **Frequently Asked Questions**

**Q: Does my Threads account need to be public?**Yes. Your Threads account must be public for publishing via Social Planner.

**Q: Why can’t I add a location to my Threads post?**Location tagging isn’t available—this option is currently limited by the Threads API.

**Q:****Does Threads support analytics in Social Planner?**

Yes. You can view Posts, Likes, Comments, and Engagement rate.

**Q: Do I need a separate Threads login?**

No. Authentication runs through Instagram (OAuth 2.0) for the Threads API. You connect the Instagram account linked to your Threads profile.

**Q: Can I mix images and video in one post?**

Yes. Carousels can include a mix of images and/or videos, up to 20 total items.

**Q: What is the text limit for Threads posts, and what happens if I exceed it?**

Threads posts can have up to 500 characters. Text over the limit is cut off, not continued as a reply. To add more text, use the Follow-up comment field. It's published as a reply directly under your Threads post.

****Q:**What happens when I post to Threads and other channels together?**

One post sent to several channels shares one caption, so the caption is limited to the smallest character limit among the selected channels. With Threads selected, Instagram, Facebook and LinkedIn captions are also limited to 500 characters. To keep each channel's full limit, turn on Customize for each channel in the editor, or import Threads posts in a separate CSV.

**Q: What happens if my Instagram/Threads token expires?**

Your scheduler will prompt you to Reconnect the Threads account; re-authenticate and scheduled posts resume.

**Q: Can I edit or delete a Threads post from Social Planner after publishing?**

Editing is not supported by Threads. You can delete posts natively from the Threads app.

**Q: Can I schedule Threads posts for multiple accounts at once?**Yes, as long as each Threads account is connected and public, you can cross-schedule to multiple Threads accounts.

---

### **Related Articles**

title_en: WordPress - LeadConnector Plugin Hub
source_md:
WordPress Integration

# LeadConnector WordPress Plugin Hub

Access a dedicated hub for downloading and managing all LC WordPress plugins, ensuring reliable availability and easy updates.

What You'll Learn

LeadConnector WordPress plugins have a dedicated home at [wordpress.leadconnectorhq.com](http://wordpress.leadconnectorhq.com), providing users with a reliable source for downloading and sharing the latest plugin versions.

This article covers how to access the plugin hub, which plugins are available, and the benefits of using this dedicated channel alongside WordPress's official plugin directories.

## What is the WordPress Plugin Hub?

The WordPress Plugin Hub is a dedicated platform hosted at [wordpress.leadconnectorhq.com](https://wordpress.leadconnectorhq.com) where users can download, use, and share the latest versions of LC WordPress plugins. This hub serves as a reliable, always-available alternative to traditional plugin distribution channels.

The plugin hub operates in parallel with WordPress's official plugin directories, giving users access to the same plugin updates through multiple channels. This dual-channel approach ensures continuous availability and reduces the risk of access disruptions.

Users can access all current LC WordPress plugins from the hub, with additional plugins planned for future release. The platform provides direct download links and version information for each available plugin.

## Key Benefits of WordPress LC Plugin Hub

**Reliable Access** — The hub provides a consistent source for all LC WordPress plugins, avoiding potential disruptions from third-party platform policies or delistings.

**Always Available** — Users can download plugins at any time without depending solely on WordPress's official directories, ensuring continuous access to critical integration tools.

**Latest Versions** — The hub maintains current versions of all plugins in sync with official directory updates, giving users immediate access to the most recent releases.

**Easy Sharing** — Teams can share direct download links with clients or team members, simplifying plugin distribution across multiple WordPress installations.

**Centralized Resource** — All LC WordPress plugins are organized in one location, making it easier to find and manage the tools needed for WordPress integrations.

## Available Plugins

The WordPress Plugin Hub currently hosts three LC WordPress plugins, with more planned for future addition.

Plugin 1

LeadConnector

The core bridge between WordPress and your CRM. Sync leads instantly and integrate custom forms without touching a line of code.

Plugin 2

LeadConnector Migrator

Seamlessly transfer data and settings between platforms. Built to handle complex migrations without losing your data.

Plugin 3

Visibility

The bridge between Visibility and WordPress. Push SEO recommendations and AI search optimizations to your site — no code required.

![](https://jumpshare.com/share/IbBzljKKwQu1Yg4i9NhZ+/Screen+Shot+2026-08-10+at+21.21.27.png)

## How to Download Plugins from the Hub

Follow these steps to download LC WordPress plugins from the dedicated hub.

Step 1

Navigate to the Plugin Hub

Visit [**wordpress.leadconnectorhq.com**](https://wordpress.leadconnectorhq.com) in your web browser. The homepage displays all available LC WordPress plugins with version information and download options.

![](https://jumpshare.com/share/IbBzljKKwQu1Yg4i9NhZ+/Screen+Shot+2026-08-10+at+21.21.27.png)

Step 2

Download the Plugin File

Click the download button for your selected plugin. The plugin file downloads as a .zip archive to your computer's default download location.

![](https://jumpshare.com/share/Xt4l8lrrMJF4FKV4uiHj+/Screen+Shot+2026-08-10+at+21.39.15.png)

Step 3

Install the Plugin in WordPress

Log into your WordPress admin dashboard, navigate to Plugins > Add New, click "Upload Plugin," select the downloaded .zip file, and click "Install Now." Once installed, activate the plugin from the Plugins page.

## Frequently Asked Questions

Q: Do I still need to download plugins from WordPress's official directory?

No. The WordPress Plugin Hub provides the same plugin versions available on WordPress's official directory. You can download plugins from either source. The hub serves as an alternative distribution channel maintained in parallel with the official directory.

Q: Will the plugins receive automatic updates if I download them from the hub?

Plugin update behavior depends on how your WordPress site is configured. Plugins downloaded from the hub function identically to those installed from WordPress's official directory. You can manually update plugins by downloading the latest version from the hub and reinstalling, or configure automatic updates through WordPress's standard update mechanisms.

Q: Can I share plugins downloaded from the hub with clients?

Yes. You can share the plugin hub URL (wordpress.leadconnectorhq.com) with clients or team members, or download plugin files and distribute them directly. The hub exists specifically to make plugin sharing and distribution more convenient.

Q: What happens if a plugin is delisted from WordPress's official directory?

The WordPress Plugin Hub continues to provide access to all LC plugins regardless of their status on WordPress's official directory. This prevents disruptions to your WordPress integrations and ensures continuous availability.

Q: Are the plugins on the hub the same versions as those on the official WordPress directory?

Yes. The plugin hub is maintained in parallel with WordPress's official plugin directory, meaning both sources receive the same updates simultaneously. You always get the latest version regardless of which source you use.

Q: How often are plugins updated on the hub?

The hub receives plugin updates at the same time as WordPress's official directory. When LC releases a new plugin version, it becomes available on both distribution channels simultaneously.

Q: Will more plugins be added to the hub in the future?

Yes. Additional LC WordPress plugins are planned for future release on the hub. The platform currently hosts LeadConnector, LeadConnector Migrator, and Visibility, with more integrations coming.

title_en: Launchpad Contextual In-App Nudges
source_md:
Contextual In-App Nudges help users complete onboarding tasks by displaying relevant guidance directly within HighLevel.

This article explains when nudges appear, what resources they can include, and how they support the onboarding experience.

---

**TABLE OF CONTENTS**

- [What are Contextual In-App Nudges?](#What-are-Contextual-In-App-Nudges?)
- [Key Benefits of Contextual In-App Nudges](#Key-Benefits-of-Contextual-In-App-Nudges)
- [Dynamic Contextual Link Options](#Dynamic-Contextual-Link-Options)
- [Automatic Nudge Suppression](#Automatic-Nudge-Suppression)
- [Example Contextual In-App Nudges](#Example-Contextual-In-App-Nudges)
- [Frequently Asked Questions](#Frequently-Asked-Questions)
- [Related Articles](#Related-Articles)

---

## **What are Contextual In-App Nudges?**

Contextual In-App Nudges automatically appear during onboarding when HighLevel detects that additional guidance may help you complete a setup task. Depending on your progress, a nudge may display one or more relevant resources—such as support articles, tutorial videos, implementation calls, or Support AI—to help you continue without interrupting your workflow.

---

## **Key Benefits of Contextual In-App Nudges**

This feature is crafted to enhance the user experience by reducing friction and delivering help at just the right moment. Its benefits include:

- Reducing onboarding friction by offering immediate, context-sensitive support.
- Driving higher action completions on LaunchPad, which contributes to improved trial-to-paid conversions.
- Providing personalized assistance through dynamic links that directly address where users are stuck.
- Enhancing overall user satisfaction by streamlining the onboarding process with minimal interruption.

---

## **Dynamic Contextual Link Options**

Dynamic Contextual Link Options integrate multiple support resources into one seamless nudge, ensuring that users find the exact help they need without leaving their workflow. This approach optimizes self-service by connecting users directly to relevant assistance.

- **Support Article** – Directly opens detailed documentation for in-depth guidance.
- **Tutorial Video**– Offers visual, step-by-step instructions for a more intuitive learning process.
- **Kickoff/Implementation Call Link** – Simplifies scheduling of personalized implementation or strategy sessions.
- **Chat with Support AI**– Provides real-time interactive support to quickly resolve issues.

---

## **Automatic Nudge Suppression**

Automatic Nudge Suppression refines the user experience by eliminating redundant prompts. When any user within a sub-account successfully completes a particular action, all contextual nudges for that action are automatically suppressed for everyone in the sub-account.

This smart function minimizes distractions and ensures that nudges only appear when truly needed.

---

## **Example Contextual In-App Nudges**

Getting started with Contextual In-App Nudges is straightforward since the feature is automatically rolled out on a going-forward basis for all plans. Follow these steps to observe and benefit from the feature in your HighLevel account:

1. Log in to your HighLevel account and navigate to the LaunchPad section.
2. Begin an onboarding action—whether that’s starting a guided tour, watching a tutorial, or engaging with a flow.
3. When you pause, abandon, or linger during an action, a contextual nudge will appear featuring one or more dynamic links.

Click on any available link (Support Article, Tutorial Video, Kickoff/Implementation Call, or Chat with Support AI) to immediately access the assistance you need.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155054711823/original/JIDc4Y6-jthBRUCCrmOa__8FNNThJxaA9g.png?1758909181)

---

## **Frequently Asked Questions**

**Q. When do Contextual In-App Nudges appear?**

Contextual In-App Nudges may appear when a user starts an onboarding or LaunchPad-related action but does not complete it, leaves the flow, or spends additional time on a tutorial or setup task.

**Q. What can a Contextual In-App Nudge include?**

A nudge may include one or more helpful resources, such as:

- A relevant support article
- A tutorial video
- A kickoff or implementation call link
- Chat with Support AI

The resources shown can vary depending on the context.

**Q. Why am I not seeing a Contextual In-App Nudge?**

You may not see a nudge if:

- The related onboarding action has already been completed.
- Another user in the same sub-account has completed the action, causing the nudge to be suppressed.
- LaunchPad is not available for your current plan, sub-account, or user role.
- The system has not detected a need to show a contextual nudge.

**Q. Why did a nudge disappear?**

Contextual nudges are automatically suppressed once the related action is completed.

If any user in the same sub-account completes the action, the related nudge may be removed for all users in that sub-account.

**Q. Will every nudge show the same resources?**

No. Contextual nudges can display different resources depending on the action or task being completed.

A nudge may include one or more relevant links rather than showing every available resource each time.

**Q. Can I manually trigger a Contextual In-App Nudge?**

Contextual nudges are displayed automatically based on user activity and onboarding progress. They are not manually triggered by the user.

**Q. Can I dismiss a nudge?**

If the current product behavior allows users to dismiss the nudge, keep the existing documented behavior here. If dismissal is not explicitly documented, I would avoid adding this FAQ until the behavior is confirmed.

**Q. Why does another user in my sub-account no longer see the nudge?**

Nudge suppression applies at the sub-account level. Once the related action is completed by any user in the sub-account, the associated nudge may be suppressed for everyone in that sub-account.

---

## **Related Articles**

- [LaunchPad Overview](https://help.gohighlevel.com/en/support/solutions/articles/155000005494)
- [Getting Started with Agency LaunchPad](https://help.gohighlevel.com/en/support/solutions/articles/155000005494)
